**C14 — source-reviewed**

The public CEL function evaluates Bulirsch complete elliptic integral cel(kc,p,a,b) using a duplication iteration, transforming the p<=0 branch before iteration. The integral definition is explicitly given in source. This mapping covers the reusable special-function routine, not the domain-specific magnetic-field APIs or a claim of all elliptic-integral forms. Source finding: the kc=0 branch tests local B before assigning B_IN, so that branch reads undefined state; the declaration already requires nonzero kc. The loop has no explicit iteration limit/status output. Positive p and nonzero kc avoid the inspected singular-branch issue; the negative-p branch is not presented as an ordinary nonsingular integral.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

bmdfsaneacc::dfsaneacc solves a square system: the residual callback maps x(n) to res(n), with no Jacobian callback. It combines residual-direction nonmonotone steps with QR-based sequential-secant acceleration built from iterate/residual history. Success requires dot_product(res,res)<=epsf**2, so epsf bounds the residual Euclidean norm; iteration exhaustion is a distinct return. F2 is already a GAMS leaf: there is no official derivative-free or acceleration child to add. Internal least-squares acceleration is not evidence for a general rectangular least-squares solver, and this does not enumerate all roots or certify uniqueness. The Fortran example supplies a three-variable exponential system; the reviewed Fortran path does not require running R or CUTEst. Memory/rank limits, singular cases and the author example were not tested.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `2e879f8b0baf7de75de8382e65d619b02bc5c7b6`.

Required residual-subroutine interface: evalr(n,x,res,pdataptr), with an optional C_PTR data handle. The residual vector has the same length as x.

Public entry point `bmdfsaneacc::dfsaneacc`: [dfsaneacc-in-Fortran/src/dfsaneacc/dfsaneacc.f90:25–39](https://github.com/johngardenghi/dfsaneacc/blob/2e879f8b0baf7de75de8382e65d619b02bc5c7b6/dfsaneacc-in-Fortran/src/dfsaneacc/dfsaneacc.f90#L25-L39).

Public module subroutine for square nonlinear systems. Supply n residuals for n REAL(KIND=8) unknowns through evalr; x is updated and res, iter, fcnt and istop are returned. epsf controls the residual 2-norm, ndiis the acceleration interval and nhlim the history capacity. pdataptr is optional.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dfsaneacc(evalr, n, x, res, epsf, maxit, ndiis, nhlim, &
               iter, fcnt, istop, pdataptr)
```

Argument declarations: [dfsaneacc-in-Fortran/src/dfsaneacc/dfsaneacc.f90:25–39](https://github.com/johngardenghi/dfsaneacc/blob/2e879f8b0baf7de75de8382e65d619b02bc5c7b6/dfsaneacc-in-Fortran/src/dfsaneacc/dfsaneacc.f90#L25-L39).

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The ACRS interface accepts finite lower/upper bounds and an objective-value callback, with no gradient or Hessian callback. Its Price iteration randomly selects working-set points, computes a weighted centroid/reflection, projects onto the box and replaces a worse objective value. G2i describes this global nonconvex search; there is no finer GAMS subclass here. Bounds are restricted by implementation checks (lower bounds must exceed -1e6 and upper bounds must be below 1e16). Termination by objective spread, iteration count or CPU budget does not certify global optimality. The supplied acrs_main/FUNCT_ACRS example is a possible future driver starting point; it was not run.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed real adjac_double path records local first-derivative dependencies in module-wide tape arrays. Multiplication records the product rule through sum_taylor_a; get_dense_jacobian_a seeds dependent variables in blocks and traverses those dependencies backward to assemble Jacobian rows. adjac_set_independent seeds variable indices. This establishes operator-overloaded first differentiation, not higher derivatives or a numerical finite-difference method. The scoped review covers real variables and dense extraction; complex, sparse-COO, tapeless and FFT variants remain outside this source mapping. The shared storage and mode flag require coordinated lifecycle management and are not independently thread-local. Reset without product_mode preserves the previous mode. Fatal errors STOP rather than return status. No numerical derivative test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `0b75bb2e52de1ace8edb7a9ef114791ea04e43f2`.

Reset shared tape indices before registering independent variables. Explicitly pass product_mode=.false. for the dense-Jacobian path; omitting it preserves the last mode. Existing AD values tied to an earlier tape must not be reused after resetting.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL adjac_reset(product_mode)
```

```fortran
call adjac_get_dense_jacobian(y, jac)
call adjac_free()
```

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

Public TRAPECIO/SIMPSON generics dispatch to private precision-specific functions. The reviewed DP paths sort finite bounds, repeatedly halve trapezoid spacing (SIMPSON extrapolates (4*Tnew-Told)/3), stop on absolute change below EPS and restore reversed-bound signs. This is automatic finite-interval function quadrature, not a grid-only routine or general singular/infinite-interval guarantee. EPS defaults to 1e-2 and is an absolute successive-estimate test, not a rigorous error bound. MAXITER=26 is fixed; nonconvergence prints and STOPs the host process. Equal-zero estimates can cause early acceptance; no oscillatory-integrand or floating-point edge tests were run. Other Integration module algorithms and imported Linear routines remain outside this source review.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `f5617d7b40109a79e70a7bfa2161b701f5b541a2`.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

setup forms segment slopes, extrapolated endpoint slopes and Akima weighted nodal slopes, then local cubic coefficients; interp selects an interval and evaluates its cubic. This establishes univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation. abs_smooth rounds the absolute-value weights when delta_x is positive, so that variant differs from unsmoothed Akima. The source assumes ordered distinct nodes and at least three points without checking them. Queries outside the data range continue the nearest end polynomial; this is not a reliable general extrapolation method. No shape-preservation, monotonicity or accuracy guarantee is inferred from the README, and no spline was run.

External evaluator returning values, argument derivatives and data sensitivities. All coefficient-sensitivity matrices are required, shaped (npt-1,npt); transpose the appropriate SETUP_DV direction blocks as the Python wrapper does. Output data sensitivities have shape (n,npt). Out-of-range queries use the nearest end polynomial.

```fortran
CALL interp(npt, n, x, xpt, p0, p1, p2, p3, dp0dxpt, dp1dxpt, dp2dxpt, dp3dxpt, dp0dypt, dp1dypt, dp2dypt, dp3dypt, y, dydx, dydxpt, dydypt)
```

External tangent-mode constructor specialized to the spline setup. Supply xptd and yptd as (nbdirs,n) seed arrays; each coefficient derivative is (nbdirs,n-1). Use positive delta_x for smooth data sensitivities. It is not a general differentiation engine for arbitrary user functions.


Argument declarations: [src/akima.f90:173–186](https://github.com/andrewning/akima/blob/b72e0f6272b8b9721141b7130b8628d6554b6958/src/akima.f90#L173-L186).

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The Tapenade-generated SETUP_DV propagates caller-supplied tangent directions through slope differences, smoothed Akima weights and cubic coefficients. interp then forms analytic derivatives with respect to the query argument and original abscissae/ordinates, including the derivative of the local coordinate. The Python wrapper seeds 2*n directions with identity/zero blocks and transposes their coefficient sensitivities. This mapping is differentiation of this particular interpolant, not a general-purpose AD package, finite-difference estimator or derivative of an unknown sampled function. delta_x is held fixed; its derivative is not computed. Positive smoothing is needed for the intended smooth data sensitivities. No derivative comparison was executed.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The reviewed UVIPIA general path (ND>=5) locates successive intervals, estimates endpoint derivatives from weighted neighboring three-point slope estimates, forms cubic coefficients for NP<=3 or higher-degree basis factors, and evaluates the corresponding interval polynomial. This supports univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation E1a, not a global polynomial, spline-system solve or smoothing fit. Ordered distinct XD is checked; invalid input prints a message and leaves YI at -9999 without a status argument. End extrapolation is linear, using endpoint slope estimates. The sketch uses NP=3 and ND=7; selecting larger NP does not establish higher-order derivative-estimate accuracy or shape preservation. Material findings: the general query loop unconditionally prints the OpenMP thread number and query index; the separate ND=4 cubic a3 formula repeats yuse(1) in its second term where the distinct second ordinate would be expected. That small-data branch requires checking/correction and is excluded from the sketch. No accuracy, small-data case or OpenMP execution was verified.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `67875afd0df120590a49e1ef3a3fc25b5b3eaab5`.

External REAL(KIND=8) interpolation subroutine. NP, ND and NI are default INTEGER, XD/YD have length ND and XI/YI length NI. XD must be strictly increasing; XI can be unordered. The inspected general path requires ND>=5. NP<3 is promoted to three. Compile/link with OpenMP support because omp_lib and omp_get_thread_num are used even apart from directive handling. There is no success/status output.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL uvipia(np, nd, xd, yd, ni, xi, yi)
```

Argument declarations: [src/uvipia_omp.f90:45–75](https://github.com/NRLMMD-GEOIPS/akima86/blob/67875afd0df120590a49e1ef3a3fc25b5b3eaab5/src/uvipia_omp.f90#L45-L75).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: uvipia
integer, parameter :: nd=7, ni=2
integer :: i
real(8) :: xd(nd), yd(nd), xi(ni), yi(ni)
xd=[(real(i-1,8),i=1,nd)]
yd=xd*xd
xi=[1.5d0,4.5d0]
call uvipia(3,nd,xd,yd,ni,xi,yi)
```

Uncompiled fragment for in-range queries and seven nodes. Expected quadratic values are 2.25 and 20.25, but no comparison was performed. Do not treat -9999 as an unambiguous failure status because it can also be a legitimate data value. The pinned general path writes per-query thread/index diagnostics. The four-node cubic branch has a source-formula discrepancy and is not demonstrated. There is no missing-data treatment or monotonicity/positivity guarantee established by this review.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The public DERIVATIVE generic selects private 1D/2D functions. The inspected 1D path computes centered differences with initial width one, halves the width and stops after at least five iterations when ABS(DNEW/DOLD-1)<ACC. It has a fixed 100-iteration maximum and STOPs on exhaustion. Arithmetic and callback use default REAL, not the separate precision module. Zero previous derivative estimates lead to division by zero, and a relative successive-estimate test is not a rigorous derivative error bound. The finite-difference path is numerical differentiation, not automatic differentiation or a review of the library integration/domain modules.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `958190dddfcb7b172c2667fa2d18e8446ad408e3`.

Public entry point `calculus::derivative`: [src/calculus.f90:27–71](https://github.com/alexander-mead/library/blob/958190dddfcb7b172c2667fa2d18e8446ad408e3/src/calculus.f90#L27-L71).

Public module generic; inspected scalar 1D binding returns default REAL and takes a default-REAL callback F(X), point X and accuracy control ACC. The callback input has INTENT(IN). Import DERIVATIVE, not the private DERIVATIVE_1D specific.

Usage:

```fortran
VALUE = derivative(F, X, ACC)
```

Argument declarations: [src/calculus.f90:8–10](https://github.com/alexander-mead/library/blob/958190dddfcb7b172c2667fa2d18e8446ad408e3/src/calculus.f90#L8-L10).

Argument declarations: [src/calculus.f90:27–49](https://github.com/alexander-mead/library/blob/958190dddfcb7b172c2667fa2d18e8446ad408e3/src/calculus.f90#L27-L49).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use calculus, only: derivative
real :: value
! Supply F(t)=exp(t) with a matching default-REAL scalar interface.
value = derivative(f,1.0,1.0e-4)
! Compare independently with exp(1.0).
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Choose controls appropriate to default REAL and a sufficiently smooth function. Do not use a zero/near-zero derivative to assume the relative test is safe. The routine can terminate the calling program and gives no status/error estimate. The author build mentions FFTW for the full library, but that is not a dependency of this inspected module body.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

**G — documentation-reviewed**

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `aa4ddb9d92c20f5d00679542f4c1d54852edbc4d6069a60bbd9a1f92309330eb`.

**G1b1c — source-reviewed**

The arp::arp_solve path is unconstrained (zero general constraints, unbounded variable arrays) and evaluates user gradient and Hessian callbacks for p=2 or p=3, adding user third-derivative tensors for p=3. arp_model::model_evalf constructs a quadratic/cubic Taylor model with cubic/fourth-order regularization; model minimization delegates to bundled ALGENCAN. G1b1c is the most specific available GAMS class for the reviewed second-/third-order modes: there is no third-derivative child. This is not automatic differentiation, and the p=3 default needs more than the first and second derivatives named by the class. The sparse and dense fourth-order regularizers have different formulas in source; numerical equivalence is not asserted. The advertised p=1 mode, generic constrained problems, and all bundled ALGENCAN algorithms are outside this mapping. No optimizer or author MGH driver was executed.

Initialize algorithmic defaults in an arp_param structure. The default derivative order is p=3. This routine does not connect the user objective and derivative procedure pointers; attach them before calling arp_solve.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL arp_load(param)
```

Argument declarations: [src/arp.f08:17–19](https://github.com/johngardenghi/ar4/blob/0f8ffc1b2701a4f5c5fd00facb8cd28c5b518026/src/arp.f08#L17-L19).

Public entry point `arp::arp_solve`: [src/arp.f08:44–53](https://github.com/johngardenghi/ar4/blob/0f8ffc1b2701a4f5c5fd00facb8cd28c5b518026/src/arp.f08#L44-L53).

Public module solver for unconstrained minimization. x is an assumed-shape REAL(KIND=dp) initial point overwritten by the result; param is an arp_param and output an arp_output. The mapped p=2/3 paths require gradient and Hessian callbacks; p=3 additionally requires third derivatives. Model minimization delegates to ALGENCAN.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL arp_solve(x, param, output)
```

Argument declarations: [src/arp.f08:44–53](https://github.com/johngardenghi/ar4/blob/0f8ffc1b2701a4f5c5fd00facb8cd28c5b518026/src/arp.f08#L44-L53).

Argument declarations: [src/arp_types.f08:97–147](https://github.com/johngardenghi/ar4/blob/0f8ffc1b2701a4f5c5fd00facb8cd28c5b518026/src/arp_types.f08#L97-L147).

Author example (not run): [drv/mgh.f08:144–170](https://github.com/johngardenghi/ar4/blob/0f8ffc1b2701a4f5c5fd00facb8cd28c5b518026/drv/mgh.f08#L144-L170).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use arp, only: arp_load, arp_solve, arp_param, arp_output
! Declare param/output with these types and initialize x.
call arp_load(param)
param%p = 2
param%dense = .true.
param%uevalf => my_evalf
param%uevalg => my_evalg
param%uevalh => my_evalh
call arp_solve(x, param, output)
```

Calling sketch for the reviewed dense p=2 path, not a complete driver. Implement compatible objective, gradient and Hessian procedures with explicit interfaces as declared in arp_types; attach procedure pointers before solving. arp_load leaves these pointers for the caller to set. Sparse or p=3 modes require their corresponding callbacks. Follow upstream build instructions for ALGENCAN and optional numerical dependencies. Not compiled or run for this catalog.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected src/avd.f90 implementation propagates derivatives through overloaded products and elementary-function composition. The avd_d4 inheritance chain stores a value and first through fourth raw derivatives with respect to one scalar parameter; the product and Q4_f chain rules contain the corresponding binomial/composition coefficients. This is forward differentiation, not finite differencing or symbolic expression manipulation. CALL init() must populate the module function-pointer table before elementary functions are used. H1 is the differentiation leaf; there is no finer automatic-differentiation child in this taxonomy. The review covers the fourth-order product/exponential path, not every overload or the older root autodiff.f90 implementation. Source requests an eight-byte default REAL build; module and caller settings must agree. No author tests or derivative comparisons were executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `a594392a9a2f6820a2b217547620dc36af46e35b`.

Public exponential generic, scoped here to the avd_d4 overload. Input/output contain v and d1..d4 in REAL(8). Seed an independent scalar with d1=1 and higher derivatives zero; extract the same fields from the result. These are raw derivatives, not factorial-scaled Taylor coefficients.

Usage:

```fortran
y = exp(x)
```

Argument declarations: [src/avd.f90:1026–1030](https://github.com/sgeard/autodiff/blob/a594392a9a2f6820a2b217547620dc36af46e35b/src/avd.f90#L1026-L1030).

```fortran
! Read y%v and y%d1 through y%d4.
```

Uncompiled fragment for the src/ implementation. Build module and caller with consistent eight-byte default REAL options as requested by the source. Initialization is shared module state; no concurrent-initialization behavior was checked. The linked author test exercises fourth-order arithmetic/trigonometric expressions, not this particular exponential fragment.

Implementation evidence `AVD::d4_times_d4`: [src/avd.f90:376–410](https://github.com/sgeard/autodiff/blob/a594392a9a2f6820a2b217547620dc36af46e35b/src/avd.f90#L376-L410).

Implementation evidence `AVD::Q4_f`: [src/avd.f90:732–790](https://github.com/sgeard/autodiff/blob/a594392a9a2f6820a2b217547620dc36af46e35b/src/avd.f90#L732-L790).

**E1b — source-reviewed**

The reviewed CGL path generates Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes mapped to [a,b], produces alternating barycentric weights with half endpoint weights, and evaluates a single univariate global Lagrange polynomial by the barycentric quotient. A near-node isclose test returns the stored sample rather than dividing by a small node difference. E1b records a single polynomial, not a piecewise interpolant or noisy-data fit. n is polynomial degree and arrays need n+1 elements despite some abbreviated shape comments. bary_weights only implements CGL weights, so the sketch does not combine it with CG/CGR nodes. Explicitly pass is_descending=.false.: the node generator default flag has declaration initialization and therefore retains a prior supplied value between calls. Positive n, distinct endpoints and adequate array extents are caller responsibilities; no error estimate/status is returned. Module imports require MKL BLAS95/F95_PRECISION even though this reviewed scalar interpolation path uses no BLAS operation. No interpolation result, extrapolation behavior or alternate node family was verified by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `6cf9f7de551072ba71435052b850d57371157394`.

Public module subroutine generating n+1 weights for CGL nodes, in the same ascending ordering as the sketch. n is the degree, not the number of elements. Supply a REAL(rp) array of length n+1; arbitrary nodes and CG/CGR weights are not implemented here.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL bary_weights(n, w)
```

Argument declarations: [src/chebyshev_m.f90:909–918](https://github.com/saridut/chebpak/blob/6cf9f7de551072ba71435052b850d57371157394/src/chebyshev_m.f90#L909-L918).

Public entry point `chebyshev_m::lag_intrp`: [src/chebyshev_m.f90:944–976](https://github.com/saridut/chebpak/blob/6cf9f7de551072ba71435052b850d57371157394/src/chebyshev_m.f90#L944-L976).

Public module barycentric interpolation function. x, w and f each need n+1 REAL(rp) elements. Source documents ascending x. A query sufficiently close to a node returns its sample directly, using relative tolerance 1e-12 and absolute tolerance 1e-14. Otherwise the weighted numerator is divided by the weight sum.

Usage:

```fortran
value = lag_intrp(n, x, w, f, p)
```

Argument declarations: [src/chebyshev_m.f90:944–960](https://github.com/saridut/chebpak/blob/6cf9f7de551072ba71435052b850d57371157394/src/chebyshev_m.f90#L944-L960).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use constants_m, only: rp
use chebyshev_m, only: cheb_node, bary_weights, lag_intrp
integer, parameter :: n=4
real(rp) :: x(0:n), w(0:n), f(0:n), value
call cheb_node("CGL",-1.0_rp,1.0_rp,n,x,is_descending=.false.)
call bary_weights(n,w)
f=x*x
value=lag_intrp(n,x,w,f,0.25_rp)
```

Uncompiled fragment; expected value is 0.0625, but no comparison was performed. Build/link the full library with compiler-compatible MKL Fortran 95 interfaces as documented upstream. Use matching CGL nodes and weights and do not assume n means array length. The code supplies no interpolation-error bound or duplicate-node check. Multivariate interpolation, quadrature and differentiation routines remain outside this source review.

Implementation evidence `utils_math_m::isclose`: [src/utils_math_m.f90:227–267](https://github.com/saridut/chebpak/blob/6cf9f7de551072ba71435052b850d57371157394/src/utils_math_m.f90#L227-L267).

## chol-rev

**License: MIT AND BSD-3-Clause-Open-MPI**

LICENSE explicitly places the four derived Fortran reverse routines under the reproduced LAPACK terms, including the third-party intellectual-property disclaimer, while other repository files use MIT. The combined expression describes those recorded components; linked BLAS/LAPACK and other third-party dependencies retain their own terms.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1`.

[LICENSE](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/LICENSE)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `d73fdd5663672185d489775cfdda74cb12e15e931051b2f5db0a7857769cda77`.

**H1 — documentation-reviewed**

The README documents the adjoint primitive that propagates factor sensitivities to the original positive-definite matrix. This is not classified as a general-purpose Cholesky solver or a complete automatic-differentiation system.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1`.

[README.md](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `89df696f996361d2b7f620e461b13bd564390cc0d0462b73067528adc0731c6d`.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

DPO2FT walks the lower Cholesky factor backward, propagating supplied factor adjoints through diagonal division, BLAS matrix/vector updates and diagonal halving. DPOFRT performs the corresponding blocked updates and delegates diagonal blocks to DPO2FT. This is a reverse first-derivative primitive for a scalar objective depending on an already-computed positive-definite Cholesky factor, not a factorization, solve or complete automatic-differentiation system. Only UPLO=L is implemented in the nonempty paths; the upper branches call XERBLA without reliably setting the advertised INFO=-8. Input checks omit LDC, so the caller must enforce it. The blocked path may overwrite entries above the selected triangle. Preserve the author triangular-adjoint convention when passing sensitivities onward. BLAS/LAPACK support routines and matching integer ABI are required. No adjoint identity or finite-difference comparison was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1`.

[dpo2ft.f](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpo2ft.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `f164d2eadd978690a864992a114e4f9b6906a4cd246996ac3407ea21a0524ff7`.

[dpofrt.f](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpofrt.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `2d21cdf4b3a31e599566461696e3baf86763b20ddae9fb9d5fc199ae95a83f2c`.

[python/chol_diff.py](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/python/chol_diff.py)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `8d3363a140bc7cd162077a6b6e162f71b80c44381094725ce3ec1ac506e20f98`.

Public entry point `DPO2FT`: [dpo2ft.f:1–164](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpo2ft.f#L1-L164).

External unblocked double-precision reverse primitive. A holds a valid lower Cholesky factor; C holds the lower factor sensitivities on entry and is overwritten with input-matrix sensitivities in the author triangular convention. Supply UPLO=L, N >= 0 and both leading dimensions >= MAX(1,N); check INFO. A and C must be separate valid arrays.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DPO2FT(UPLO, N, A, LDA, C, LDC, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [dpo2ft.f:9–15](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpo2ft.f#L9-L15).

Author example (not run): [python/chol_diff.py:153–166](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/python/chol_diff.py#L153-L166).

Public entry point `DPOFRT`: [dpofrt.f:1–219](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpofrt.f#L1-L219).

External blocked variant with the same double-precision input/output convention, lower-factor restriction and required leading dimensions. Calls DPO2FT for small problems and diagonal blocks. C is modified in place, including some upper entries; retain only the meaningful triangle. INFO is not an accuracy estimate.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DPOFRT(UPLO, N, A, LDA, C, LDC, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [dpofrt.f:9–15](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/dpofrt.f#L9-L15).

Author example (not run): [python/chol_diff.py:261–274](https://github.com/imurray/chol-rev/blob/d85b1e3c00650a11d79b9305c75682646e83cac1/python/chol_diff.py#L261-L274).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dpofrt
double precision :: factor(2,2), adjoint(2,2)
integer :: info
factor = reshape([2.0d0,1.0d0,0.0d0,3.0d0],[2,2])
adjoint = 0.0d0
adjoint(1,1) = 1.0d0
adjoint(2,2) = 1.0d0
call dpofrt("L",2,factor,2,adjoint,2,info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "reverse Cholesky failed"
```

Uncompiled calling sketch. The supplied lower factor defines X=factor*transpose(factor); adjoint initially seeds the sum of the factor diagonal. Link these reverse routines with ABI-compatible BLAS and LAPACK support; this is not a standalone single-file program. The output uses the author triangular sensitivity representation, so do not automatically symmetrize or double off-diagonals without matching the subsequent contraction convention. No numerical check was performed.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

[Pinned discovery list](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Fortran-code-on-GitHub/blob/f5ab25294a12ed004d5a8934200ca8e26ac2e825/README.md).

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The public BRENTZERO generic selects single/double bindings. The reviewed double binding tests endpoint roots/signs, maintains a bracket, attempts secant or inverse-quadratic interpolation and falls back to bisection when acceptance conditions fail. It returns an interval-scale convergence test or exact computed zero, evaluation count and explicit error code. The routine is for one continuous scalar equation with a sign-changing bracket, not guaranteed root enumeration, polynomial complex roots or discontinuous functions. The initial FA*FB sign test can overflow/underflow, and finite values/positive tolerances/iteration limits are not validated. No accuracy or pathological-bracket behavior was checked by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1`.

[fmm.f90](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `f2c3d0c63b0e126cd093df644f9720e16e50b8eb56e5219a418a5b9e4c634a10`.

Public entry point `ForsytheMalcolmMoler::BrentZero`: [fmm.f90:3076–3223](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L3076-L3223).

Public module generic; reviewed double binding uses SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50). Callback F(X) has a scalar real input with INTENT(IN) and scalar real result. ERRCode=0 normal, 1 iteration budget, 2 endpoints have the same sign; NEVAL counts endpoint and iteration evaluations.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL BrentZero(AX, BX, F, TOL, MAXITER, NEVAL, ERRCODE, XZERO, FZERO)
```

Argument declarations: [fmm.f90:83–85](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L83-L85).

Argument declarations: [fmm.f90:103–104](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L103-L104).

Argument declarations: [fmm.f90:3076–3095](https://github.com/Beliavsky/Computer-Methods-for-Mathematical-Computations/blob/b850d06d29e348a803feaba58c0b68a8fdd5c5f1/fmm.f90#L3076-L3095).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: BrentZero
integer, parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50)
real(dp) :: root, residual
integer :: neval, status
! Provide F(x)=x*x-2 with a matching REAL(dp) scalar interface.
call BrentZero(1.0_dp,2.0_dp,f,1.0e-10_dp,100,neval,status,root,residual)
if (status /= 0) error stop "BrentZero failed"
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Provide the callback, finite endpoint values, a continuous bracketed problem and positive controls. Compare ROOT with sqrt(2) and independently evaluate the residual. Convergence in bracket width is not a universal residual guarantee; ERRCODE=2 returns HUGE sentinels. No other textbook solver is promoted to source-reviewed by this mapping.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

## ConFlow

**Z — documentation-reviewed**

The README describes a problem-specific flow-field generator with binary/HDF5 maps for downstream transport models. SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `589ed823e9a84c56feb95ac58e7cf384626b9cbf4fda2a907bc36e103de1bad2`.

[cwt.f90](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `d74e06262b985149dc0312c97f01249b4a917ac605dcef2e4bc1472fd7bfd3d8`.

**J — documentation-reviewed**

The brief README identifies a Fortran 90 signal-transform program and these two wavelet families. Normalization conventions, boundary treatment and numerical accuracy need source/example review; other wavelet families are not inferred.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da`.

[README.md](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `713fff5a4ce63453e02eb5d67f18c7c412730eb0168f4136c549c956c1c28f39`.

**J — source-reviewed**

The inspected program evaluates Morlet or Mexican-hat kernels at each integer scale and translation, multiplies by sampled signal and applies a trapezoidal weighted sum before writing coefficient magnitudes. This is a direct demonstrative continuous-wavelet-transform implementation, kept in the verified broad integral-transform class J rather than inventing a finer wavelet code. Quadrature omits time-step factors, translations use sample indices rather than input times, and the Morlet path uses default COMPLEX even though times are real(kind=8). No inverse transform, phase-preserving output, arbitrary-grid normalization or acceleration is established. Internal procedures belong to the program and are not reusable public module interfaces. File/allocation controls are not robustly validated; a malformed input can STOP the process.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da`.

[cwt.f90](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `d74e06262b985149dc0312c97f01249b4a917ac605dcef2e4bc1472fd7bfd3d8`.

[cwt.par](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.par)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `b8672c34274885cda13a0d131328053897a3df30cd496b3e56414e6ffe1fcedc`.

Program entry point `cwt`: [cwt.f90:1–236](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.f90#L1-L236).

Standalone PROGRAM, not a linkable module API. Command argument 1 names a four-line parameter file; absent argument prompts for a file name. The program reads an input basename plus .dat and writes a prefixed scalogram file. Its contained wavelet/quadrature functions are internal helpers.

Usage:

```fortran
cwt PARAMETER_FILE
```

Argument declarations: [cwt.f90:18–27](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.f90#L18-L27).

Argument declarations: [cwt.f90:34–57](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.f90#L34-L57).

Argument declarations: [cwt.f90:208–234](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.f90#L208-L234).

Author example (not run): [cwt.par:1–4](https://github.com/khaors/CWT/blob/a24daaa6d0cf8910100ada29f0290721367362da/cwt.par#L1-L4).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
gfortran cwt.f90 -o cwt
./cwt cwt.par
```

Invocation sketch only; no compilation or execution was performed. Supply the four parameter records: input basename, output prefix, number of scales, wavelet selector (0 Morlet / 1 Mexican hat). Input .dat starts with sample count followed by time/value rows. The supplied cwt.par references CO1.dat. Output coefficients are magnitudes only. Treat time as unit-spaced sample coordinates and validate normalization independently; internal helpers do not use actual time differences in quadrature.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected serial DCTSV solves real square cyclic tridiagonal systems with multiple right-hand sides by paired endpoint elimination, small determinant solves for the even/odd terminal cases, and back substitution. DL(1) stores the top-right corner and DU(N) the bottom-left corner. Those corners make this a general real system rather than an ordinary tridiagonal matrix in the displayed ordering; D2a1 is used without implying a dense factorization. D/DL/DU are read-only and B is overwritten by solutions. N>=4 and leading-dimension checks precede work. No pivoting is implemented; exact-zero intermediate determinant checks do not prove singularity of the entire matrix, and INFO=0 is not a conditioning or accuracy certificate. The README recommends diagonal dominance and warns that error grows faster with N than LU. This review excludes general wider-band and OpenMP variants. No solve, residual or timing comparison was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a`.

External double-precision cyclic tridiagonal solver. Supply N>=4, NRHS>=0, DL(N), D(N), DU(N), and B(LDB,NRHS), with LDB>=N. The wrapped corner elements are part of DL/DU. B becomes the solution; diagonals are preserved. Check INFO, but also assess residuals independently. Link XERBLA (normally supplied by LAPACK).

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DCTSV(N, NRHS, DL, D, DU, B, LDB, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [dctsv.f90:55–73](https://github.com/mostlyharmlessone/cyclic-banded-matrix/blob/939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a/dctsv.f90#L55-L73).

Argument declarations: [dctsv.f90:10–39](https://github.com/mostlyharmlessone/cyclic-banded-matrix/blob/939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a/dctsv.f90#L10-L39).

Author example (not run): [testme.f90:162–176](https://github.com/mostlyharmlessone/cyclic-banded-matrix/blob/939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a/testme.f90#L162-L176).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dctsv
integer :: info
double precision :: dl(4), d(4), du(4), rhs(4,1)
dl=-1.0d0
d=4.0d0
du=-1.0d0
rhs(:,1)=2.0d0
call dctsv(4,1,dl,d,du,rhs,4,info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "cyclic elimination failed"
```

Uncompiled fragment for a strictly diagonally dominant cyclic system with expected constant solution one. No residual was checked. Retain a copy of the original RHS for that check. This routine does not return reusable LU factors. Default INTEGER and double precision must match the linked error-handler ABI; positive INFO is an elimination-breakdown indication, not proof that every possible solver would fail.

**D2a2a — source-reviewed**

The separate external thomas routine performs forward elimination and backward substitution for an ordinary real tridiagonal system with k right-hand sides. The lower diagonal a(i) is read for i=2..n, the upper c(i) for i=1..n-1; a(1) and c(n) are unused. It overwrites b and d while returning solutions in z. This supports D2a2a (ordinary tridiagonal systems), not periodic corner coupling. There is no pivoting, dimension validation or error-status output, and division by zero or small elimination pivots is not guarded. Use appropriate nonzero-pivot inputs; no stability theorem or numerical check is established by this source inspection.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a`.

[thomas.f90](https://github.com/mostlyharmlessone/cyclic-banded-matrix/blob/939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a/thomas.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `f1f35ad444a28759333558d85d61c483e4045496a2d8e76b15e08b1c5c9d13e7`.

Public entry point `thomas`: [thomas.f90:1–19](https://github.com/mostlyharmlessone/cyclic-banded-matrix/blob/939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a/thomas.f90#L1-L19).

External nonpivoted tridiagonal elimination. n and k are default INTEGER; a/b/c are double-precision length n arrays, d and z have shape (n,k). b and d are overwritten; a/c are declared INOUT but not changed in the inspected body. z receives the solution. There is no INFO argument.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL thomas(a, b, c, d, z, n, k)
```

Argument declarations: [thomas.f90:1–8](https://github.com/mostlyharmlessone/cyclic-banded-matrix/blob/939e8e32bfcebf4676bb83cfe410ec6d3419c34a/thomas.f90#L1-L8).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: thomas
double precision :: a(4), b(4), c(4), rhs(4,1), z(4,1)
a=-1.0d0
b=4.0d0
c=-1.0d0
rhs(:,1)=[3.0d0,2.0d0,2.0d0,3.0d0]
call thomas(a,b,c,rhs,z,4,1)
```

Uncompiled fragment for an ordinary diagonally dominant tridiagonal system, with expected constant solution one. This does not use cyclic corner entries. Keep copies of b and rhs for residual checks; zero/near-zero elimination pivots are not reported safely. Neither this routine nor the cyclic routine was benchmarked.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

SENZADERGLOB constructs bounded random trial points and uses an exponential acceptance threshold before derivative-free local searches. RICERCA_LUNGO_ASSI delegates to box-search kernels; linesearchbox_cont enforces bounds and sufficient objective decrease using only function values. This supports global nonconvex optimization (G2i), not a requirement to provide derivatives. The inspected routine is a working-set implementation; its title does not establish an MPI/distributed-memory interface. Evaluation/step limits and comparisons with a supplied fglob are stopping criteria, not proofs of a global minimum. The upstream MAIN_GLOB driver and repeated-run statistics were not executed.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

dirdfn combines a DIRECT-type global partition search with CS-DFN local minimizations. The inspected nuovoglobale block invokes sd_box and subdivides potentially optimal rectangles; objective and feasibility are tracked separately through value-only callbacks. Finite lower and upper bounds are required, as the author driver explicitly warns. This global constrained search maps to the G2i leaf; finite evaluation/interval budgets and a supplied target fglob do not certify a global optimum or feasibility. The author main_test/problem example is available as a future driver candidate, not a checked example.

External subroutine for bounded, generally constrained global search. It returns xbest and uses separately linked objective/constraint routines and shared modules rather than callback arguments. The initial xbest is replaced by the box midpoint. Bounds must be finite; maxnf is INTEGER*8, nomefun has length 40 and numerical vectors use REAL*8.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dirdfn(n, me, mi, xbest, lb0, ub0, nomefun, iprint, &
            maxint, maxnf, fglob, tolglob)
```

Argument declarations: [DIRDFN.f90:22–41](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/DIRDFN/blob/3776d1d4e71abf371f2f143493ab48cb1affaadc/DIRDFN.f90#L22-L41).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
! Compile upstream modules and your problem.f90 definitions first.
! Set dimensions, finite bounds, budgets and target-value controls.
call dirdfn(n, me, mi, xbest, lb, ub, nomefun, iprint, &
            maxint, maxnf, fglob, tolglob)
```

Calling sketch only. Follow the author main_test for variable kinds and supply the upstream problem routine interfaces (funob, fconstreq and fconstrin). This is not a stateless callback API: shared modules and output units are used. A desired objective target and tolerance do not certify a global minimum. Not compiled or run for this catalog.

**G2h3b2 — source-reviewed**

The local sd_box implementation is explicitly CS-DFN for nonsmooth nonlinear programming. It uses coordinate/dense search directions and value-only objective/constraint evaluation, while funct_pen adds positive inequality violations and absolute equality violations. funct_vinc calls both fconstrin and fconstreq. This supports G2h3b2, the leaf for general nonlinear functions with equality and inequality constraints without a smoothness assumption. Nonsmooth does not establish convergence for arbitrary discontinuities: regularity assumptions, penalty updates and numerical convergence remain unverified. The supplied problem contains nonlinear polynomial equalities; its existence is not a successful solve.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `3776d1d4e71abf371f2f143493ab48cb1affaadc`.

**G — documentation-reviewed**

**G2i — source-reviewed**

nuovoglobale evaluates an objective-value callback on a bounded domain, selects potentially optimal rectangles and triggers sd_box local searches after the configured trigLS budget fraction. The local kernel projects its starting point onto bounds and uses function-value line searches; no user derivative interface is present in the inspected path. G2i is the most specific GAMS global nonconvex class. Internal discrete-search branches in the shared local-search source are not enough to advertise an integer-programming solver: index_int is initialized to zero. **H1 — source-reviewed**

The dnadmod dual type carries a default-REAL value x and a derivative vector dx(ndv). Reviewed real assignment zeroes the vector, dual multiplication applies the product rule, and exp_d multiplies the seed vector by exp(x). The public entry is the exp generic; exp_d and mult_dd are private specifics. This is first-order forward automatic differentiation, with the derivative-vector length chosen at preprocessing time by ndv (default one), not a higher-order derivative or finite-difference implementation. Seed every derivative component explicitly for independent inputs and compile callers against the matching module. The header notes default single precision unless consistent compiler options promote default REAL. No derivative result was checked by execution.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The real dual-number path propagates first derivatives in a dx(ndv) vector through overloaded multiplication, division, exponential and sine operations. The inspected product, quotient and chain-rule formulas operate on values and derivative vectors, without finite-difference steps. auto_fill seeds identity derivatives separately for concentration and spatial-gradient variables, then extracts flux/reaction/accumulation Jacobian entries. This supports H1, already a GAMS leaf including automatic differentiation. It is forward first-order differentiation, not a Hessian or reverse-mode implementation. In this fork ndv=2*N depends on user_input, and the scalar real kind follows the build configuration; it is not a standalone precision-generic package without adaptation. The reviewed path does not establish correctness of every overload, complex extensions or nondifferentiable branches. The README credits inherited DNAD by Wenbin Yu/Maxwell Blair and the upstream fork; those components are not newly attributed to this repository. No derivative check or program was executed.

**D2a2 — source-reviewed**

ABDGXY assembles neighboring real blocks and BAND performs forward block elimination followed by back substitution, including special boundary couplings through X and Y. Each block solve delegates to MATINV, which applies Gaussian/Gauss-Jordan row operations to B and the multiple right-hand sides in D. The supported GAMS scope is real nonsymmetric banded linear systems (D2a2). Block tridiagonal structure is not generally scalar tridiagonal, and boundary terms can reach an additional neighboring block, so the D2a2a leaf would overstate the structure. This is an inherited Newman BAND-style specialized solver using module-global arrays, not a general LAPACK-compatible band-storage interface. NJ must accommodate the referenced neighboring nodes, and the routine assumes compatible block/boundary assembly. Singular-block diagnostics print and continue in BAND; conditioning, pivot robustness, residuals and larger systems were not checked. No complex or symmetric-positive-definite specialization is inferred.

**I2a1a — source-reviewed**

This mapping is restricted to the simple rectangular diffusion example, not the repository collection of physical applications. The author program sets one dependent variable, one spatial grid and a positive constant diffusivity; FLUX=-diff*dc/dx, RXN=0 and ACCUM=c/delT describe the one-dimensional parabolic diffusion initial-boundary problem. auto_fill forms finite-volume flux/accumulation derivatives; unsteady loops over spatial nodes through auto_fill/ABDGXY/BAND and updates the solution in time, with prescribed end concentrations. I2a1a is the GAMS leaf for parabolic PDEs in one spatial dimension. The example uses absolute author-machine include paths, and BAND_MOD uses another absolute path, so it is a source example requiring path adaptation rather than a portable checked driver. The included core wiring is inspected, but boundary compatibility, time accuracy, stability and mesh convergence were not checked. No general nonlinear iteration-convergence guarantee or multidimensional PDE mapping is added.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The root CALC_DQ_COEFF generic dispatches to coefficient generators; the reviewed real_kind binding constructs Gaussian RBF matrices and differentiated right-hand sides using variable precision/hyper-dual arithmetic, calls LDL_SOLVE, adapts width/precision and rescales derivative weights. This is a numerical-differentiation weight service, not automatic differentiation of an arbitrary user function. It supports named first/second coordinate derivatives and mixed derivatives on 3-coordinate point stencils. Duplicate nodes and unknown derivative strings are not guarded; optional Taylor indices need valid bounds. A precision failure sets STAT but output coefficients are still copied. Only this root variable-precision path was reviewed, not the separate native-precision examples or every arithmetic/linear-solve kernel.

## easydop853

**License: BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause**

The pinned LICENSE reproduces three-clause BSD notices for Jiachen An and Jacob Williams and the two-clause BSD notice for Ernst Hairer. These component notices are retained rather than presenting only the wrapper copyright. The source also reproduces the wrapper notice.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289`.

[LICENSE](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/LICENSE)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `918b9a6af63c29af81ffd7694ed045026ef17b00505fbe9df6017dbbcb41feb4`.

[easydop853_module.f90](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/easydop853_module.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `311246097018ed07ad21e2e826c8a21e5beb6655b08eef7b4f94ba0b186cd8b4`.

**I1a — documentation-reviewed**

The README describes a simplification of Jacob Williams DOP853 interfaces. Users cannot set tolerances and other parameters through this simplified interface; complete configurability of the original is not claimed.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289`.

[README.md](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `678f4a551814c2a79b33ca075663204447807d76a3d20d7575450266bd7de4c3`.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected easydop853 wrapper initializes a DOP853 object and integrates a callback-defined initial-value system. The reviewed core evaluates explicit Runge-Kutta stages, scales embedded error estimates by absolute/relative tolerances, accepts or rejects steps and clips the last step to the requested endpoint. This is a one-step nonstiff method; stiffness detection is not a stiff solver. The wrapper fixes rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-24, nmax=2250000 and nstiff=1 and requests no output callback or dense output. It converts initialization and negative integration statuses into ERROR STOP rather than exposing a recoverable flag. It returns only the final x and y and exposes none of the configurable lower-level tolerance/statistics interface through its argument list. Local error control does not certify global accuracy. Other dense-output and event modes are outside this review. No orbit, decay test or error estimate was checked by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `22b1ee81da0568573731caffab9c4316af5ea6aa10aff2dd497248dccc83dd2c`.

Public entry point `easydop853_module::easydop853`: [easydop853_module.f90:49–84](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/easydop853_module.f90#L49-L84).

Module subroutine with real64 x as initial/final independent variable, real64 xend as requested endpoint, and an INOUT real64 state vector y(:). Callback fcn(me,x,y,f) must include class(dop853_class) me and assumed-shape state/derivative vectors, even if it does not use the object. Fixed tolerances cannot be changed through this interface. Failure ERROR STOPs; no idid is returned.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL easydop853(fcn, x, xend, y)
```

Argument declarations: [easydop853_module.f90:53–59](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/easydop853_module.f90#L53-L59).

Argument declarations: [dop853_module.f90:160–168](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/dop853_module.f90#L160-L168).

Author example (not run): [easydop853_test.f90:9–22](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/easydop853_test.f90#L9-L22).

Author example (not run): [fcn.f90:1–20](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/fcn.f90#L1-L20).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use easydop853_module, only: easydop853, deriv_func, wp
procedure(deriv_func) :: decay
real(wp) :: x, y(1)
x = 0.0_wp
y = 1.0_wp
call easydop853(decay,x,1.0_wp,y)
```

Uncompiled calling fragment. Supply decay(me,x,y,f) matching deriv_func, with f=-y for the test equation; its analytic endpoint is exp(-1), but no comparison was run. Compile dop853_constants, dop853_module and easydop853_module in that order before the caller/callback. The wrapper returns only endpoint values; use the lower-level object interface if configurable tolerances, dense output, statistics or recoverable error handling are needed.

Implementation helper `dop853_module::dp86co`: [dop853_module.f90:608–709](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/dop853_module.f90#L608-L709).

Callback `dop853_module::deriv_func`: [dop853_module.f90:160–168](https://github.com/GasinAn/easydop853/blob/3749d517cddd998e5338f49208b6b10f7d12b289/dop853_module.f90#L160-L168).

**C14 — source-reviewed**

The inspected public complete_elliptic_integrals wrapper returns complete first-/second-kind integrals. For 0<=m<1 it dispatches associated Fukushima integrals and forms K=B+D, E=B+(1-m)*D; m=1 has explicit infinite K/unit E, and m>1 uses reciprocal-parameter/complement transformations for complex outputs. Input is parameter m=k*k, unlike modulus-input libraries. Negative m returns NaNs and is not supported. C14 records elliptic-integral evaluation; public incomplete/Jacobi entries and full associated-integral arithmetic remain unreviewed. The build uses REAL128 internally even for REAL64 outputs. Exact equality/branch-cut, near-singular and extreme-parameter accuracy was not validated. This is a wrapper/transformation review, not a complete kernel audit or execution test.

Public elemental elliptic-module subroutine. REAL(dp) parameter M; COMPLEX(dp) outputs FC (complete K) and EC (complete E). DP=REAL64; QP=REAL128 internally. For the illustrated 0<=M<1 branch output imaginary parts are zero. There is no status argument; negative M gives NaNs and M=1 uses a complex-infinity representation for FC.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL complete_elliptic_integrals(m,Fc,Ec)
```

Argument declarations: [source/ellipFor_modules/elliptic.f90:121–140](https://github.com/seantrim/ellipFor/blob/c1ecd389b0a571813e98c0d92013def279b00e93/source/ellipFor_modules/elliptic.f90#L121-L140).

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `3adb5648e31a72c019e81f05545b36a8642304ec`.

[README.md](https://github.com/DSCF-1224/elliptic_k_using_agm_fortran/blob/3adb5648e31a72c019e81f05545b36a8642304ec/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `0d3e3a29ed03fabf935dedcc52d7ae6aed613ce4866a7ef1816352f0fb8795e3`.

**C14 — source-reviewed**

The inspected REAL64 elliptic_k overload evaluates the complete Legendre elliptic integral of the first kind with modulus k. It forms the complementary modulus as sqrt((1-k)*(1+k)); for k*k<0.5 it returns (pi/2)/AGM(1,k-prime), and otherwise uses an AGM/elliptic-nome logarithmic transformation. C14 is the elliptic-integrals leaf in this taxonomy; complete first-kind scope is recorded in the procedure rather than inventing a narrower code. IEEE branches return quiet NaN for NaN input or |k|>1 and positive infinity for |k|=1. Material limitation: although the interface advertises |k|<=1, the second branch calls arithmetic_geometric_mean_kernel(1,k), not AGM(1,abs(k)); negative k with k*k>=0.5 therefore reaches a signed-input dependency path and must not be assumed valid. The sketch uses nonnegative modulus and the simple direct branch. Dependencies are unpinned Git references in fpm.toml, and their full AGM/nome algorithms are outside this review. The committed module unconditionally imports/declares REAL128 as well as REAL32/64, so its build needs that kind despite README calling it optional. No integral or reference test was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `3adb5648e31a72c019e81f05545b36a8642304ec`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `7bb2510b327f42ce279a29f0c39cf69fe930201b29fbaaf9e72c5aef8cbc4c9a`.

**D — documentation-reviewed**

Documents exp(t*A), exp(t*A)v and phi-function actions for dense and sparse matrices. Linear algebra is supported; a more specific matrix-function mapping awaits procedure review.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `db906c01150025eec83654b42feb66c5f09960a9`.

[README](https://github.com/rasmusgo/expokit/blob/db906c01150025eec83654b42feb66c5f09960a9/README)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `06301738b4db1db1a0b81f3b0b4cb907d36fa456cf5eee7744467ec912e9158a`.

**D8 — source-reviewed**

The inspected real dense DGPADM routine scales t*H, evaluates the diagonal Pade rational approximation using matrix products and a linear solve, then repeatedly squares the result. It returns the full exp(t*H) through an offset into caller workspace. D8 follows the published NAG GAMS convention grouping matrix functions with other matrix equations (the NAG D8 index lists real matrix exponentials); this is not a claim of a general Sylvester-equation solver. Only this dense real path is reviewed: sparse Krylov exponential actions, complex variants and phi-functions are not certified here. Invalid sizes, zero norm of t*H (including t=0 or H=0), and linear-solve failure STOP rather than returning a recoverable error. The caller must handle identity cases and provide valid positive dimensions and workspace. No matrix exponential, conditioning or scaling-extreme test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `db906c01150025eec83654b42feb66c5f09960a9`.

[fortran/dgpadm.f](https://github.com/rasmusgo/expokit/blob/db906c01150025eec83654b42feb66c5f09960a9/fortran/dgpadm.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `f5c2879d93626538e985e692478b438d7ba4346918e839d1c1f08eb9671cf530`.

Public entry point `DGPADM`: [fortran/dgpadm.f:2–169](https://github.com/rasmusgo/expokit/blob/db906c01150025eec83654b42feb66c5f09960a9/fortran/dgpadm.f#L2-L169).

External double-precision dense matrix exponential. Use positive m, ldh >= m, recommended ideg=6, ipiv(m) and wsp length >= 4*m*m+ideg+1. exp(t*H) occupies wsp(iexph:iexph+m*m-1) in column-major order; iexph is one-based relative to the passed workspace. ns reports squarings. Handle t=0 or H=0 outside the routine because its zero-norm branch STOPs. Link compatible BLAS/LAPACK.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DGPADM(ideg, m, t, H, ldh, wsp, lwsp, ipiv, iexph, ns, iflag)
```

Argument declarations: [fortran/dgpadm.f:4–6](https://github.com/rasmusgo/expokit/blob/db906c01150025eec83654b42feb66c5f09960a9/fortran/dgpadm.f#L4-L6).

Argument declarations: [fortran/dgpadm.f:26–40](https://github.com/rasmusgo/expokit/blob/db906c01150025eec83654b42feb66c5f09960a9/fortran/dgpadm.f#L26-L40).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dgpadm
integer, parameter :: m=2, ideg=6, lwsp=4*m*m+ideg+1
integer :: ipiv(m), iexph, ns, iflag
double precision :: h(m,m), work(lwsp), exponential(m,m)
h = 0.0d0
h(1,1) = 0.1d0
h(2,2) = 0.2d0
call dgpadm(ideg,m,1.0d0,h,m,work,lwsp,ipiv,iexph,ns,iflag)
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "matrix exponential failed"
exponential = reshape(work(iexph:iexph+m*m-1),[m,m])
```

Uncompiled calling sketch. The analytic reference is diag(exp(0.1),exp(0.2)), but no comparison was run. The result is the full matrix exponential, not entrywise exponentiation or just its action on a vector. Link ABI-compatible BLAS/LAPACK; some failures terminate inside DGPADM before the iflag check can run. The chosen nonzero matrix/time avoids its identity-case STOP.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

**H — documentation-reviewed**

The README specifies equally spaced real/complex samples and returns the integral divided by the interval length, so callers must supply interval scaling themselves. Extrapolation requires 2^M+1 samples; other lengths use trapezoidal reduction, and a singleton is returned unchanged. Stated error orders and edge cases were not independently checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `5472eb6f2b85c5ff2337f3e52acd2d689335c078`.

[README.md](https://github.com/irukoa/Extrapolation_Integration/blob/5472eb6f2b85c5ff2337f3e52acd2d689335c078/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `b1877e726065257766909b178c0a80815b890c52f79b18d92b9d4d4cd02bc3ba`.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed real(dp) extrapol_rdp path accepts equally spaced samples rather than an integrand callback, error tolerance or adaptive sampling request. It reorders 2^m+1 samples with endpoints first, constructs nested trapezoidal approximations and applies Richardson extrapolation. H2a1b2 is the nonautomatic finite-interval grid-quadrature leaf. The reduction is normalized to [0,1]; multiply by (b-a) for samples on [a,b], as the author sinc example does. A material fallback discrepancy was found by source inspection: non-dyadic sample counts are sent directly to trap_rdp, which half-weights array(1) and array(2), not the first and last samples in natural order. For [0,1/3,2/3,1] the displayed formula predicts 11/18 instead of the trapezoidal result 1/2; this is an arithmetic consequence of the source, not a compiled result. Singleton/two-point cases have separate branches; empty input and all accuracy claims remain unverified. No checked driver is supplied.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `5472eb6f2b85c5ff2337f3e52acd2d689335c078`.

Public generic array-reduction function. The inspected REAL(dp) binding accepts an assumed-shape vector and returns a scalar of the same kind; extrapol_rdp and its nested helpers are private implementation details. Supply equally spaced samples with 2**m+1 entries for the reviewed extrapolation path, and multiply the normalized result by the physical interval length.

```fortran
result = extrapolation(array)
```

```fortran
use Extrapolation_Integration_Kinds, only: dp
use Extrapolation_Integration, only: extrapolation
! array is REAL(dp) with 2**m+1 equally spaced samples on [a,b].
result = (b - a) * extrapolation(array)
```

**K5 — source-reviewed**

CSPLINE forms second differences of equally spaced observations, factors a structured smoothing system using an untruncated or truncated recurrence, reconstructs the fitted values, evaluates a GCV-style score and fills intermediate/end samples. K5 records smoothing rather than exact interpolation through the supplied data. The user supplies LAM; returning SCORE does not mean the routine automatically minimizes GCV or chooses LAM. T enters through LAM*T**3, R selects subdivision/output layout and JJ controls recurrence truncation. There are no argument checks or status output. Small N and truncated recurrence sizes can cause invalid indexing; divisions/logarithms and score trace need valid nondegenerate inputs. The source review does not establish a general admissible parameter region or numerical stability.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `9878445007a84cdb69b79d3c1cdc5c5e00c23f05`.

Public module subroutine using REAL*8. Y(N) is input, X(R*N+R-1), XONY(N) and SCORE are outputs. Fitted original-node values occupy X(R:R*N:R); other entries are intermediate samples and end extensions. This is a regular-grid routine, not an arbitrary-abscissa spline API.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL cspline(X, XONY, SCORE, Y, N, R, T, JJ, LAM)
```

Argument declarations: [cspline.f90:4–20](https://github.com/jamesorr/fastspline/blob/9878445007a84cdb69b79d3c1cdc5c5e00c23f05/cspline.f90#L4-L20).

```fortran
use mcspline, only: cspline

integer :: j
y = [(real(j,kind(1d0)),j=1,n)]
call cspline(x,fitted,score,y,n,r,0.1d0,6,5.8d0)
```

REAL*8 is a compiler extension; confirm its kind matches the compiled module. Do not infer that LAM=0 is safe or that any positive N/R is accepted. **J1a2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected ZFFT1D driver initializes twiddle tables with IOPT=0, factors supported lengths into powers of 2/3/5, and dispatches the complex FFT235 radix passes directly or through a blocked two-factor decomposition for larger vectors. IOPT=-1 selects the forward transform; IOPT=1 conjugates before the same FFT and conjugates/scales by 1/N afterward for the inverse. J1a2 records one-dimensional complex discrete Fourier transforms. The source requires N=2**p*3**q*5**r; FACTOR does not return an unsupported-factor error, so callers must validate the positive length themselves. B has 2*N complex entries and holds both scratch and coefficients. Large-path WX/WY tables are SAVE state: initialize again for the current length and do not assume independent large-length setups can be interleaved. Compiled param.h dimensions bound decomposition axes and no runtime bounds/status validation is supplied. Review covers the driver, factorization and radix dispatch, not every kernel, OpenMP behavior, MPI/GPU variants or numerical accuracy. No transform or round-trip was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `33b3400dcf9ced8576ce12282932ce772bdf0062`.

Public entry point `ZFFT1D`: [zfft1d.f:32–85](https://github.com/certik/ffte/blob/33b3400dcf9ced8576ce12282932ce772bdf0062/zfft1d.f#L32-L85).

External in-place complex-double FFT driver. A needs N entries, B needs 2*N entries; INTEGER N/IOPT must match the fixed-form build ABI. Initialize with IOPT=0, then use -1 forward or +1 inverse. Forward output is unscaled; inverse includes 1/N. Only positive 2/3/5-smooth lengths are supported, with additional compiled workspace-size constraints. There is no status dummy.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL ZFFT1D(A, N, IOPT, B)
```

Argument declarations: [zfft1d.f:18–39](https://github.com/certik/ffte/blob/33b3400dcf9ced8576ce12282932ce772bdf0062/zfft1d.f#L18-L39).

```fortran
a=cmplx(0.0d0,0.0d0,kind(0.0d0))
a(1)=cmplx(1.0d0,0.0d0,kind(0.0d0))
call zfft1d(a,n,0,work)
call zfft1d(a,n,-1,work)
! For this impulse the unscaled spectrum is all ones.
call zfft1d(a,n,1,work)
```

Uncompiled small-path fragment. No spectrum or round-trip comparison was performed. Build/link zfft1d.f, fft235.f, kernel.f and factor.f with a consistent param.h include and compatible COMPLEX*16/default INTEGER conventions; the upstream test Makefile shows that source set and OpenMP flags. Retain the coefficient part of work between calls, reinitialize when changing length, and do not assume shared large-path tables are reentrant. The sample avoids unsupported prime factors and large decomposition dimensions.

Implementation evidence `FACTOR`: [factor.f:19–43](https://github.com/certik/ffte/blob/33b3400dcf9ced8576ce12282932ce772bdf0062/factor.f#L19-L43).

Counts powers of 2, 3 and 5 without returning a validation status for remaining prime factors.

**J1a3 — source-reviewed**

The inspected FFTL entry reweights logarithmically spaced samples, dispatches FHTQ and postscales using logarithmic spacing, bias, kr and rk. FHTI initializes FFTPACK and complex-Gamma transform coefficients. With mu=+1/2 or -1/2 this is the logarithmically sampled sine/cosine transform subset J1a3, not a conventional equally spaced FFT or a certified infinite-domain quadrature. FHTI setup can be reused only while N/mu/q/spacing/kr stay fixed. Its OK flag is not a full validation certificate (N<=0 can still reach OK=true), so validate positive N, nonzero spacing and positive kr/rk. The command-line driver restricts mu to +1/2 despite a cosine hint in an error message, and applies its own physical normalization. Lower-level FHTQ, FFTPACK and complex-Gamma arithmetic are outside this review. No transform, ringing or round-trip check was run.

External REAL*8 setup. N/KROPT default INTEGER; MU/Q/DLNR/KR real double; KR may be adjusted. KROPT=1 selects quiet low-ringing adjustment. WSAVE needs 2*N+2*(N/2)+18 for Q=0, or 2*N+3*(N/2)+19 otherwise. Check logical OK and validate inputs independently.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL fhti(n,mu,q,dlnr,kr,kropt,wsave,ok)
```

Argument declarations: [fftlog.f:233–236](https://github.com/coccoinomane/fftlog-f90/blob/85c617abac1a6536f124f9bcc00b37b0f3cc9cec/fftlog.f#L233-L236).

Public entry point `fftl`: [fftlog.f:473–562](https://github.com/coccoinomane/fftlog-f90/blob/85c617abac1a6536f124f9bcc00b37b0f3cc9cec/fftlog.f#L473-L562).

External in-place transform of A(N). DIR=+1/-1 forward/backward; initialize WSAVE with FHTI first, using MU=+0.5 for sine or -0.5 for cosine. RK is r_center/k_center, not the product KR. Output uses the logarithmic grid and sqrt(2/pi) sine/cosine normalization documented here, distinct from the command-line driver extra scaling.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL fftl(n,a,rk,dir,wsave)
```

Argument declarations: [fftlog.f:473–475](https://github.com/coccoinomane/fftlog-f90/blob/85c617abac1a6536f124f9bcc00b37b0f3cc9cec/fftlog.f#L473-L475).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: fhti, fftl
integer, parameter :: n=16
integer :: i
logical :: ok
double precision :: a(n), work(4*n+19), kr, rk, spacing, r
kr=1.0d0
spacing=0.1d0
call fhti(n,0.5d0,0.0d0,spacing,kr,1,work,ok)
if (.not.ok) error stop "FFTLog setup failed"
rk=1.0d0/kr
do i=1,n
  r=exp((i-0.5d0*(n+1))*spacing)
  a(i)=exp(-r*r)
end do
call fftl(n,a,rk,1,work)
```

Uncompiled interface fragment with r_center=1 and k_center=KR, so RK=1/KR after any setup adjustment. The short log range is illustrative, not an accuracy demonstration. Validate domain truncation, periodic-extension/ringing effects and grid/normalization before comparing transforms. Link FFTLOG plus bundled DRFFTI/DRFFTF/DRFFTB and CDGAMMA support. Never confuse RK ratio with KR product, or the library normalization with the CLI postprocessing.

**J1a2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D COMPLEX(real64) dcfft1/dicfft1 bindings allocate FFTW-aligned complex storage, create an in-place FFTW_ESTIMATE plan, copy input after planning, execute the forward/backward FFTW call, copy output and destroy/free the plan/buffer. The public fft/ifft generics select these specifics for complex double vectors. Forward is unscaled; inverse divides by the requested length. Optional num(1) truncates input or pads trailing zeros; output is allocatable and replaced on entry. This supports J1a2 as an interface to an external complex DFT implementation, not a new FFT-kernel audit. Each call plans afresh; there is no persistent plan/wisdom reuse in this path. Nonpositive lengths are not validated before allocation/planning, failure uses STOP 1 rather than a status result, and module/caller precision and C interoperability must match the linked FFTW build. Real, other-rank, single-precision and shift families are outside this source review. No wrapper tests, FFTW execution, scaling comparison or timing was run.

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran

use fftw3_wrapper, only: fft, ifft
complex(real64) :: input(4)

input=cmplx(0.0_real64,0.0_real64,real64)
```

Uncompiled fragment; no spectrum or round-trip error was checked. Outputs must be allocatable and must not alias the input. The distributed module references single- and double-precision FFTW symbols, so the documented build links both libfftw3 and libfftw3f and needs the FFTW fftw3.f03 include file. Use positive lengths representable in C_INT. Optional resizing changes the transformed sequence; an inverse after truncation is not recovery of discarded samples. No plan reuse or concurrency guarantee was tested.

Public entry point `fftw3_wrapper::ifft`: [source/fftw3_wrapper.f90:47–58](https://github.com/kuanchihwang/fftw3_wrapper/blob/1886e06c68a49597c964cb25a1352866936a8807/source/fftw3_wrapper.f90#L47-L58).

Public module inverse generic, scoped to dicfft1. Takes COMPLEX(real64) input, returns a separately allocated COMPLEX(real64) vector and divides by its requested transform length. Optional num(1) has the same truncation/zero-padding behavior as fft. Allocation/planning failure stops the process.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL ifft(out, inp, num)
```

Argument declarations: [source/fftw3_wrapper.f90:261–273](https://github.com/kuanchihwang/fftw3_wrapper/blob/1886e06c68a49597c964cb25a1352866936a8807/source/fftw3_wrapper.f90#L261-L273).

Specific binding is also public; the calling sketch uses the public generic fft.

**H1 — documentation-reviewed**

The source interface includes differentiation of a supplied Jacobian and explicitly selects real128. Interface inspection does not establish supported platforms, stencil accuracy or successful compilation; real128 availability is compiler-dependent.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d`.

[findiffmod.f90](https://github.com/PunchesMalone/findiff/blob/8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d/findiffmod.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `fbf138fca4448b7354d74b3d6a99a18a7ed225d92aa2ae98738d433aff715623`.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected findiff and findiff_multiscale paths perturb each coordinate and combine symmetric 3-, 5-, 7- or 9-point stencils to approximate a square vector-function Jacobian. findiffhes instead differences a supplied square Jacobian callback and returns a rank-three derivative tensor; it does not directly compute a scalar Hessian from scalar function values. The order argument selects stencil point count, not derivative order or a certified accuracy order. All reviewed interfaces use iso_fortran_env real128, require nonzero suitable perturbations and provide no automatic step selection, error estimate or status. The generic stencil fallback is three-point with a printed warning. The author test files select real64 while the module selects real128 and need consistent kinds/imports before they can serve as drivers. The matrix-in-time and multiscale-tensor paths are not included in this review. No stencil error or compilation failure was reproduced.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d`.

Public entry point `findiffmod::findiff`: [findiffmod.f90:107–201](https://github.com/PunchesMalone/findiff/blob/8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d/findiffmod.f90#L107-L201).

Module function approximating J(i,j)=d f_i/d x_j for a callback mapping an n-element real128 vector to an n-element real128 vector. xstar and scalar eps must have that kind. order is one of 3,5,7,9. Returned matrix is (n,n); eps is an absolute coordinate perturbation.

Usage:

```fortran
jacobian = findiff(f, xstar, eps, order)
```

Argument declarations: [findiffmod.f90:109–124](https://github.com/PunchesMalone/findiff/blob/8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d/findiffmod.f90#L109-L124).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use findiffmod, only: wp, findiff
real(wp) :: x(2), jacobian(2,2)
x = [1.0_wp,2.0_wp]
jacobian = findiff(my_vector_function,x,1.0e-4_wp,5)
```

Calling fragment only, not a checked driver. Supply an explicit-interface my_vector_function(x) returning real(wp) f(size(x)), with assumed-shape real(wp) input. Import wp from this pinned module, or consistently select real128; do not mix the real64 kinds used by the bundled tests. Choose and validate the step for the actual function and scale. real128 availability depends on the compiler.

Public entry point `findiffmod::findiff_multiscale`: [findiffmod.f90:280–385](https://github.com/PunchesMalone/findiff/blob/8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d/findiffmod.f90#L280-L385).

Square real128 Jacobian function with a separate absolute step epsvec(j) for each coordinate. Every step must be nonzero and chosen for the function scale; output column j uses that coordinate step. No adaptive error control is implemented.

Usage:

```fortran
jacobian = findiff_multiscale(f, xstar, epsvec, order)
```

Argument declarations: [findiffmod.f90:282–297](https://github.com/PunchesMalone/findiff/blob/8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d/findiffmod.f90#L282-L297).

Public entry point `findiffmod::findiffhes`: [findiffmod.f90:5–106](https://github.com/PunchesMalone/findiff/blob/8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d/findiffmod.f90#L5-L106).

Differentiate a user-provided real128 square Jacobian j(x). Returns tensor res(i,j,k)=d J(i,j)/d x_k using the selected centered stencil. Caller must supply the Jacobian callback; the name does not imply a direct scalar-Hessian interface.

Usage:

```fortran
tensor = findiffhes(j, xstar, eps, order)
```

Argument declarations: [findiffmod.f90:7–18](https://github.com/PunchesMalone/findiff/blob/8cd97a1605a87022553a7343f40b397f8508fb8d/findiffmod.f90#L7-L18).

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `6848d08d05e96a30bb79d8d7780b286227b706b2b8cdc879a01564d787f05174`.

**G2h3b1 — source-reviewed**

FIRD solves smooth nonlinear programs with equality/inequality constraints and variable bounds. The fird wrapper requires objective-value, constraint-value and constraint-Jacobian callbacks. dfoirfalg actually calls the user Jacobian to form linearized constraints and passes it to restoration, while the objective interface requests no derivatives. The author guide (doc/doc.tex, lines 99-123 at this revision) explicitly assumes continuously differentiable objective and constraint functions. G2h3b1 is retained deliberately: G2h3b1a would falsely imply no user derivatives, while G2h3b1b requires objective derivatives as well as constraint derivatives. No GAMS leaf exactly represents this mixed interface. Default restoration delegates to external ALGENCAN; source inspection does not establish a standalone solver or successful convergence. The HS14 author example is a future driver candidate, not a checked solve.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `16ef79b194358c20e5ffb3554c6362742de1018c`.

External wrapper for constrained minimization. Supply objective values, individual constraint values and sparse constraint Jacobians through the userinterface callback signatures. Objective derivatives are not required; constraint derivatives are required. x is updated in place; equality constraints precede inequalities.

```fortran
          verbose, ftype, epsfeas, epsopt, f, feas, fcnt, flag)
```

**E1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected type generates S separate degree-at-most-S-1 Lagrange polynomials on overlapping S-point stencils drawn from 2*S-1 nodes. compute_coefficients forms the product-form basis at one target, and compute_interpolations applies each stencil column to stored Y values, returning S estimates. E1b records single-polynomial interpolation within each stencil; the source does not choose or combine these estimates into one piecewise or WENO interpolant. Default coordinates are the integers -S+1..S-1; optional coordinates must provide the same 2*S-1 layout with distinct increasing values. S>=2 is required by the initializer accesses to x(-1), x(0) and x(1), but is not validated. The target must lie between the midpoints adjacent to x(0) and must not equal x(0); failure uses ERROR STOP. No duplicate-node, ordering or optional-array-size check is supplied, and no error estimate/status is returned. Recompute coefficients after changing coordinates/target. No polynomial reproduction or driver execution was checked.
