**H2a1a2 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed Newton-Cotes method evaluates a concrete integrand object at n+1 equally spaced nodes on a finite interval. init selects closed-rule weights for degrees 1..10, and integrate_1D performs a single fixed weighted sum without a tolerance or error estimate, supporting the nonautomatic callback quadrature leaf H2a1a2. Source finding: weights use the usual h=(b-a)/n normalization but the final multiplication uses (b-a)*k without dividing by n. Thus degrees above one appear scaled by n; the calling sketch is restricted to n=1 (trapezoidal rule). Unsupported degrees are not rejected and leave zero weights; no success status is returned. The inherited adaptive_integrate reads an INTENT(OUT) accumulator before defining it and is excluded from the calling sketch. 2D/3D bindings are empty result-returning stubs and receive no mapping. No quadrature output was run or checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `8205e064eae8e95fcc2254584061182e29590490`.

Uncompiled fragment using the author-supplied type_cos test module, which must be built with the library. This uses one trapezoidal panel, so it is not an accuracy demonstration. It deliberately avoids the higher-degree scaling issue and the separate adaptive_integrate path. There is no returned convergence status.

Callback `FORbID_adt_integrand::integrand%f`: [src/lib/forbid_adt_integrand.f90:27–38](https://github.com/giacrossi/FORbID/blob/8205e064eae8e95fcc2254584061182e29590490/src/lib/forbid_adt_integrand.f90#L27-L38).

Extend integrand and override f(self,x,y,z), retaining optional y/z arguments even for a one-dimensional function. The author cosf extension provides one example.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D Romberg path starts with the endpoint trapezoidal rule, halves the mesh, evaluates newly introduced odd nodes, and builds Richardson extrapolation columns using 4**k. It stops when the absolute difference between the last two columns meets tol, within an n-level budget, supporting automatic finite-interval callback quadrature H2a1a1. This is global refinement, not local adaptive subdivision or a proven error bound. Important source finding: if the loop exhausts its budget without EXIT, i becomes n+1 and the returned R(i,i) is outside the allocated 0:n table. Nonpositive budgets/tolerances are not validated and no failure status is returned. Resolve this exhaustion path before relying on the routine. The 2D/3D methods are unimplemented stubs and are not mapped. No integration or failure case was reproduced by execution.

**C8 — source-reviewed**

The public FERF generic selects elemental real32/real64 approximations to erf. Both inspected bindings compute SIGN(1-(1+0.278393*abs(x)+0.230389*x**2+0.000972*abs(x)*x**2+0.078108*x**4)**(-4),x). This is a fixed-coefficient approximation, not a high-accuracy replacement for intrinsic ERF, ERFC or scaled tails. Extra precision in the DP interface does not add coefficient accuracy. Squaring/polynomial powers can overflow for large inputs, and no exceptional-value handling, error estimate or status is provided. Only FERF, not the library reductions/logarithm/trigonometric approximations, is source reviewed; neither speed nor numerical error was measured.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `a4f93517a2c09c57b6ae74585404ae4457d16716`.

**N — documentation-reviewed**

The README documents intro_sort_mod and its sort interface with optional reverse order, CMake presets and example builds. Supported element kinds, worst-case behavior, stability and edge cases require source-level review. No timings or sorted-output checks were run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `0907093a66f05f1c59bee70fb82ed9e40924416d`.

[README.md](https://github.com/suzuyuyuyu/Fortran-introsort/blob/0907093a66f05f1c59bee70fb82ed9e40924416d/README.md)

**N6a2a — source-reviewed**

The sort generic dispatches to integer int8/int16/int32/int64 routines that overwrite arr, so this is active internal integer sorting (N6a2a), not passive ranking. The inspected int32 implementation and shared templates partition around a pivot, switch to binary insertion sorting for short ranges and to heapsort at the depth limit. History-enabled variants carry caller-provided labels along with moved values; they still sort arr actively. The actual module name at this pin is mod_introsort, differing from the README usage snippet. The wrapper computes log(size(arr)) before handling empty input; zero-length behavior, stability, concurrency of module max_depth and performance were not checked. No external/file sorting or character/complex-key interface is claimed.

**N8 — source-reviewed**

The public apply_permutation generic rearranges integer/real companion data by gathering temp(permutation(:)) into the output array. The inspected int32 and real64 bodies and common template support the N8 permuting leaf independently of the sorting operation. The permutation must already have the desired output-to-input convention; history arrays supplied to sort must be initialized by the caller, as the author test initializes identity labels. SAFE_MODE checks matching lengths but does not establish that entries form a valid bijection. This is not a passive ranking API or a permutation validator. No permutation or history round trip was executed.

**N6a2a — source-reviewed**

merge_sort_mod::sort overwrites default-integer vectors or reorders integer matrix columns according to a selected reference row, with optional caller-supplied history. Recursive halves are combined by merge_1i/merge_1ih using a temporary copy and a left-first <= comparison. This is active internal integer sorting (N6a2a); the history option is not a rank-only interface. The descending wrapper reverses arr without reversing history, so the ascending-history correspondence must not be assumed to survive reverse=.true. The implementation moves whole columns for 2-D input; it is not independent sorting of every row. No stability guarantee, descending-history check or author example was executed.

**N6a2b — source-reviewed**

The real(sp), real(dp) and real(qp) generic bindings overwrite a vector or permute complete matrix columns using one selected real reference row. The inspected double-precision wrappers and shared merge bodies support active internal real sorting (N6a2b). The optional history is moved during ascending merges; reverse=.true. reverses only the data in the inspected wrappers, so descending history correspondence is not verified and appears inconsistent. Real128 support, NaNs, signed-zero ordering, stability after reversal and extreme sizes were not checked. No passive-rank, character or complex-key mapping is inferred.

**N8 — source-reviewed**

The public rearrange generic applies reference_history as a gather permutation. The included 1-D body copies arr(reference_history(i)); the 2-D body copies complete arr(:,reference_history(i)) columns. Default integer and real sp/dp/qp variants are exposed. This supports the N8 permuting leaf, independently of how the permutation was obtained. The caller must supply valid indices with the correct direction; the inspected bodies do not validate a bijection or compute its inverse. The separate descending-sort history discrepancy is retained in the sorting mappings. No bounds, permutation-cycle or round-trip checks were executed.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected public fixed-step solver implements the classical four-stage explicit RK4 formula. The adaptive solver compares one full RK4 step with two half steps and accepts using an unscaled absolute maximum component difference, then adjusts the step with a fifth-root rule. Both solve a callback-defined first-order initial-value system. The fixed interface stores time/state by rows, whereas the adaptive output stores time/state by columns. The fixed routine does not guard a one-column solution buffer before dividing by n_steps-1; the adaptive routine requires a forward interval and a positive meaningful tolerance. Its discrepancy test is not a certified global error bound. I1a1a records one-step nonstiff scope. The separate VSS routine and stiff-system claims are not included in this review.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `a5e52899a189308ce78874bd55a1ec300884be83`.

Supply an associated procedure(ODE_System) pointer with callback (n,t,x,dx_dt). Preallocate solution_matrix(n_sys+1,n_steps) with n_steps >= 2; row 1 is time and the remaining rows are states. Check status. Compile MOD_Select_Kind first.

```fortran
CALL ODE_Numerical_Solve_RK4(indp_var_span, n_sys, initial_conds, ODE_System_ptr, solution_matrix, status)
```

Supply the same callback, a forward time span and positive absolute tolerance. solution_matrix must be an allocatable real(pv) array; the routine allocates it. Column 1 is time and later columns are states, unlike the fixed-step output. Check status before consuming results.

```fortran
CALL ODE_Numerical_Solve_RK4_Adaptive(indp_var_span, n_sys, initial_conds, ODE_System_ptr, solution_matrix, status, tolerance)
```

**E3 — source-reviewed**

The inspected rbf_type%build constructs a local RBF interpolation matrix for each caller-supplied neighbor stencil, obtains its inverse and forms derivative matrices from kernel evaluations. This is an interpolation service (E3), not a complete value-evaluation API: optional y is not referenced, and the routine neither fits data values nor returns values at arbitrary queries. The Gaussian unaugmented matrix path is identifiable in source; the derivative and polynomial branches need correction/checking. In particular, the Gaussian second derivative expression differs from the analytic derivative; polynomial-augmented B entries are not fully initialized before whole-matrix multiplication, and an active debug print indexes node ten without checking node count. Compile with USE_LAPACK: inverse_matrix has an empty alternative branch. Select a distance function first, validate indices and stencil nonsingularity, and use poly_order=-1 to avoid augmentation. No interpolant, derivative matrix or failure was checked by execution; no PDE-solver or general scattered-interpolator mapping is inferred.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `0e66c2452b01d1711884c1b2d70b4b854ee30ec2`.

Type-bound rbf_type constructor, with x(num_dim,num_node), ngb_idx(num_ngb,num_node), a supported kernel selector and real(r8) parameter. r8 is hard-coded kind 8. ngb_idx contains valid one-based node indices; neighbor selection is caller work. Initialize distance_mod first. Reviewed unaugmented Gaussian use sets kernel_ga and poly_order=-1. Matrices are stored on the object; y is unused and no status is returned.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL rbf%build(x, ngb_idx, kernel_type, kernel_opt, poly_order, y)
```

**F1 — documentation-reviewed**

The README distinguishes a bounded-interval scalar function solver and an nth-degree polynomial-root routine. Author test programs and advertised precision options have not been checked in this catalog.

[README.md](https://github.com/bryand4140/FORTRAN-Roots/blob/0a145fc5da74b021faf3b8576ac499e54025e439/README.md)

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The public fun_zero implementation combines secant proposals with bisection for a scalar function supplied by procedure pointer. The inspected body does not implement inverse quadratic interpolation, despite the Brent wording in its header. It requires strictly opposite endpoint signs: endpoint zeros are rejected by the initial product >= 0 test. Optional controls set absolute tolerance, iteration budget and printing. Initial NaNs have a status path, but the interior NaN check is inside the show_iterations branch. This is a nonpolynomial single-equation mapping, not an all-roots guarantee or a numerical validation.

**F1a — source-reviewed**

poly_roots builds a real companion matrix from descending-power coefficients, dividing by the leading coefficient, balances it and obtains real or complex-conjugate roots through its private real Hessenberg double-QR iteration. Degree <= 0 and zero leading coefficients have explicit error statuses; QR exhaustion also returns failure. The optional accuracy_hint is a machine-epsilon/degree/iteration/norm heuristic, not a certified root error bound. The source path establishes polynomial-root scope; repeated roots, conditioning and accuracy were not checked by execution.

## FortranConsoleSpline

**License: MIT**

The root MIT license names John Alexiou. This records the reviewed repository license and does not imply that the implementation or any numerical result has been checked by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc`.

[LICENSE.md](https://github.com/ja72/FortranConsoleSpline/blob/88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc/LICENSE.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `c804ea113ab114880535de97a759295bc806b7814d0aee7c987c7e45b143cb96`.

**E1a — documentation-reviewed**

The README documents value, first/second derivative and extremum interfaces, plus linear behavior outside the data range. Endpoint and extrapolation behavior have not been independently checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc`.

[README.md](https://github.com/ja72/FortranConsoleSpline/blob/88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `e0e73f70d5f53e49d7792e489b66b948502b36c7b6b9c7459cb1735b716528cf`.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The module constructs and evaluates a real64 univariate piecewise-cubic interpolant from ordered samples, with optional endpoint first derivatives and natural endpoint conditions when slopes are absent. The type-bound value, slope and slope2 methods evaluate the interpolant and its derivatives; outside the data range the implementation suppresses the cubic terms, giving linear value/slope extrapolation and zero second derivative. E1a is the supported polynomial-spline classification; this is not smoothing, multidimensional fitting or a generic global-extremum solver. Source inspection found a material construction discrepancy: the interior coefficient sig uses x(i)-(i-1), mixing an abscissa with an index, instead of the adjacent abscissa difference expected for the documented arbitrary-grid cubic-spline recurrence. Ordered, distinct abscissae and compatible lengths are not comprehensively validated. The extrema helper continues bisection even after its same-sign endpoint branch, so no root/extremum enumeration claim is added. Neither the author example nor interpolation accuracy was tested.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `88f138a0a8ad8e71c89237df5fc236097ab695cc`.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected array overload accumulates 0.5*(x(i+1)-x(i))*(f(i)+f(i+1)), a composite trapezoidal integral of sampled data. H2a1b2 records nonautomatic grid-data quadrature, including nonuniform spacing, not a tolerance-driven callback integrator. Caller must provide ordered nodes and matching arrays; empty/singleton arrays produce zero. The parent declares a separate callback trapezoidal_rule_f but this submodule only supplies the array body. Plain FUNCTION headers in these submodules differ from the parent MODULE FUNCTION declarations and build compatibility was not checked. Mismatch handling delegates to an unreviewed print_error_message policy. No integral or build was executed.

```fortran
use ftlib_kinds, only: dp
```

**H2a1a2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D Gaussian path obtains tabulated Gauss-Legendre nodes/weights for N=1..5, maps them affinely from [-1,1] to the first two endpoint entries, evaluates a procedure pointer and scales the weighted sum by half the interval length. H2a1a2 records nonautomatic finite-interval callback quadrature; no tolerance/error estimator is present. Unsupported N has no SELECT CASE default and leaves rule data undefined. The callback pointer must be associated, endpoints must have at least two entries, and its optional parameter-array convention must match. Plain submodule FUNCTION versus parent MODULE FUNCTION consistency needs build checking; multidimensional behavior is unreviewed. No quadrature result was executed.

[README.md](https://github.com/ckormanyos/gamma_f77/blob/56568aa9257f587c4c09f033954c3cadd5ef4666/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `8674f592fa4e48a0ccf0fbbde99e84e14408dffb4111be53ca21884b4b475439`.

**C7a — source-reviewed**

The inspected GAMMA_MOD::TGAMMA evaluates real Gamma by a 48-coefficient reciprocal-Gamma expansion in Horner form, recurrence products after reducing |X|, and reflection for negative noninteger arguments of magnitude above one. Positive integer arguments take a factorial-product branch. C7a records Gamma evaluation; no log-Gamma, reciprocal-Gamma output API, incomplete Gamma or complex extension is inferred. QP=selected_real_kind(32) requires compiler support for at least 32 decimal digits and sufficient range for the source literal 1e4000. At zero/negative integer poles the routine returns that finite sentinel rather than an IEEE infinity or status. Default-INTEGER conversions of X are not range-guarded; NaN, infinities, overflow and large recurrence products are not handled robustly. The last DATA coefficient lacks the _QP suffix used by the others, so coefficient rounding deserves checking before asserting a full precision guarantee. gamma.f also contains a main test program after the module; extract/build the module separately when linking a different main. No accuracy or pole/overflow case was executed.

A 32-digit arithmetic kind does not establish 32 correct result digits; series coefficients and error behavior were not numerically audited.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

The active rk_wrapper path selects the explicit seven-stage Dormand-Prince embedded tableau, then uses two weighted stage estimates for adaptive one-step integration of a callback-defined initial-value system. Tolerances are hard-coded to sqrt(machine epsilon), the estimator uses an L2 difference and a global maximum component scale, and accepted states use the bstar estimate. This records intended one-step nonstiff scope, not verified order or accuracy. A material source finding is that calc_k initializes dummy_y only once before the stage loop and accumulates all successive stage sums into it, instead of rebuilding each stage from y; the implemented stages therefore need correction/checking before relying on the named method. The first adaptive trial is not clipped to the interval endpoint; clipping occurs after a step. Rejection exhaustion STOPs; there is no status output. The routine writes to unit 22. Implicit/nonlinear-solver branches and their stiff suitability are not reviewed or mapped.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `eebf44cc47e9f62adf19c093d59479afda1b88ce`.

Module entry for real64 state integration. Provide num_t >= 2 increasing output times t(num_t), initialize y(1,:) in y(num_t,n), and supply dysub(n,t,y,dy) with real64 inputs/output. Usage:

```fortran
CALL rk_wrapper(n, num_t, t, y, dysub)
```

**F1 — documentation-reviewed**

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `ba82e48ffeb27a6a334e9de50da891bd790b515e`.

[README.md](https://github.com/physicsfan/GetRootsF/blob/ba82e48ffeb27a6a334e9de50da891bd790b515e/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `f615baec364ba28571932490230ab13ac4a3da74d7eb545d076daae8df4659fb`.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The public real32 scalar solvers hybridD and hybridSA implement Newton/bisection and accelerated-secant/quadratic-candidate/bisection branches respectively. Their callbacks are pure scalar functions; hybridD also requires a derivative. Source findings prevent treating these as checked solvers: hybridD updates the bracket using fx0*fx1 rather than the newly evaluated midpoint value; hybridSA tests f0*f2 when accepting x3 rather than f0*f3. Both use relative step tests that divide by the candidate root, print on bracket failure without returning a status, and expose no explicit convergence flag. The separate range-scan routine root_searchD skips the first scanning segment and refers to optional max_iters without consistently using its local default. No all-roots or correctness guarantee is recorded, and no program was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `ba82e48ffeb27a6a334e9de50da891bd790b515e`.

## gfsolver

**License: MIT-style license with citation request**

LICENSE.md is headed MIT and names Giulio Fella, but adds a numbered request to cite the package in addition to retaining the copyright/permission notice. The full pinned text is linked; no exact SPDX MIT expression is asserted for this modified notice.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432`.

[LICENSE.md](https://github.com/gfell/gf_solver/blob/0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432/LICENSE.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `eddd2042803c94eabce159079b88371720b3b25244a0ddf3a18bca91666e9dc4`.

**F1 — documentation-reviewed**

The brief README describes switching from basic Newton to a hybrid method after the iteration limit. Bracketing conditions, derivative callbacks and failure handling need further review.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432`.

[README.md](https://github.com/gfell/gf_solver/blob/0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `b6e0fbf261e47ba87fd213d044ea5b8a7859acc5d5a231f887cc2533ea522c13`.

**F1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected module solves a scalar real equation through function-value and first-derivative subroutine callbacks; the dummy vectors have length one. sub_newton takes Newton steps and attempts a sign-changing bracket after its Newton iteration limit, then calls sub_hybrid_nb, which bisects when a Newton trial leaves its current interval. F1b describes general nonpolynomial scalar root finding; this is not polynomial root enumeration, a derivative-free interface or a square-system solver. The hybrid code updates the first endpoint when f(x)<0, so its input pair must have the matching sign orientation; it does not validate a bracket on entry. Failure paths print and STOP rather than returning a status, and the Newton path divides by df before testing for a small derivative. The optional fnorm on direct Newton success stores the residual computed before the final x update. The fallback call does not forward the optional tolerance or iteration controls, so the hybrid defaults apply there. Convergence, singular-derivative behavior and all bracket assumptions were not checked by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432`.

[gf_solver.f90](https://github.com/gfell/gf_solver/blob/0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432/gf_solver.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `d3934946b86f5c0e8fd25a8d22b642827a3206f978384450a64d8b87829c8a60`.

Public entry point `mod_gfsolver::sub_newton`: [gf_solver.f90:13–141](https://github.com/gfell/gf_solver/blob/0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432/gf_solver.f90#L13-L141).

Public module Newton solver with hybrid fallback. fcn and dfcn are external subroutines called as (1,x,value), not scalar Fortran functions. xguess and x are REAL(ki) arrays of length one; tolerances, lower search limit, iteration count and fnorm are optional. ki is SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,30).

Usage:

```fortran
CALL sub_newton(fcn, dfcn, xguess, x, minx_in, errrel_in, &
                errabs_in, max_iter_in, fnorm)
```

Argument declarations: [gf_solver.f90:37–44](https://github.com/gfell/gf_solver/blob/0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432/gf_solver.f90#L37-L44).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use mod_gfsolver, only: ki, sub_newton
real(ki) :: xguess(1), x(1)
! Supply external callbacks fcn(n,x,f) and dfcn(n,x,df).
xguess = 1.0_ki
call sub_newton(fcn, dfcn, xguess, x)
```

Calling sketch only; implement compatible explicit-shape/assumed-size callback vectors and declare the callbacks appropriately in the caller. A zero/small derivative may trigger a division fault or STOP; failures can terminate the calling program. Lower-bound randomization is not a general bounded-root guarantee. Optional controls are not forwarded to the fallback hybrid call. No program was compiled or run.

Public entry point `mod_gfsolver::sub_hybrid_nb`: [gf_solver.f90:144–233](https://github.com/gfell/gf_solver/blob/0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432/gf_solver.f90#L144-L233).

Public module Newton-bisection solver. Supply a two-element REAL(ki) pair whose function values have the negative/positive orientation expected by the endpoint updates, along with both function and derivative subroutines. x is a one-element output array; optional tolerances and iteration controls have defaults.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL sub_hybrid_nb(fcn, dfcn, xguess_in, x, errrel_in, &
                   errabs_in, max_iter_in, fnorm)
```

Argument declarations: [gf_solver.f90:162–168](https://github.com/gfell/gf_solver/blob/0926b61db2c0fa3fa2e1b874ef5ac15d5d6df432/gf_solver.f90#L162-L168).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use mod_gfsolver, only: ki, sub_hybrid_nb
real(ki) :: bracket(2), x(1)
! Initialize a valid sign-oriented bracket and supply fcn/dfcn.
call sub_hybrid_nb(fcn, dfcn, bracket, x)
```

Calling sketch only. Validate the bracket and avoid a zero derivative before relying on this interface: the implementation does not supply a bracket-validation return code or a guarded derivative division. Hitting the iteration limit prints and STOPs. This review does not establish convergence or residual accuracy.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The public BILINEAR routine interpolates values from a regular rectangular input grid to query points using four tensor-product weights. It estimates uniform spacing from axis endpoints; it does not search nonuniform coordinates. DATA_IN is laid out (NY,NX) and POINTS is (NQUERY,2). The out-of-range branches contain CONTINUE rather than CYCLE, so they fall through to invalid indexing and overwrite the sentinel; upper endpoints are also unsafe. This mapping records implemented gridded interpolation, not correctness at boundaries or source review of the separate scattered-data/triangle methods.

Public module subroutine using default REAL. Require ascending uniformly spaced axes with at least two nodes each and strictly interior queries. The module imports other project modules and OMP_LIB, and prints elapsed time. The current out-of-domain handling is unsafe.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL bilinear(X_AXIS, LEN_X, Y_AXIS, LEN_Y, DATA_IN, POINTS, NUM_POINTS, DATA_IP)
```

Argument declarations: [interpolation.f90:6–12](https://github.com/ChristianSteger/grid_interpolation/blob/8d46f927432837cb379a2caa4d2eeb0b28ebadae/interpolation.f90#L6-L12).

Argument declarations: [interpolation.f90:20–38](https://github.com/ChristianSteger/grid_interpolation/blob/8d46f927432837cb379a2caa4d2eeb0b28ebadae/interpolation.f90#L20-L38).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use interpolation, only: bilinear
real :: x(2), y(2), values(2,2), points(1,2), result(1)
x = [0.0,1.0]; y = [0.0,1.0]
values(:,1) = [0.0,2.0]
values(:,2) = [1.0,3.0]
points(1,:) = [0.25,0.5]
call bilinear(x,2,y,2,values,points,1,result)
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The interior sketch samples x+2*y, whose analytic query value is 1.25; this value was not compared by execution. Reject boundary/outside queries before this routine or repair its fall-through branches. Compile/link the imported project modules and OpenMP runtime. F2PY hides length arguments, but direct Fortran callers supply them.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

**I1 — documentation-reviewed**

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3`.

**I1a1a — source-reviewed**

DOPRI5 provides an explicit embedded Dormand-Prince 5(4) method for nonstiff initial-value systems. The inspected entry checks options/workspace, configures error tolerances and dispatches the stage/acceptance/step-control core in the same file. Stiffness detection can stop integration; it is not a stiff solver. This fork adds a LOGICAL DEBUG argument between IOUT and WORK, so an unmodified upstream DOPRI5 call is incompatible. Dense output requires selected component storage and SOLOUT configuration. Only this method, not all HWODE solvers, is source reviewed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3`.

[dopri5.f](https://github.com/cpmech/hwode/blob/784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3/dopri5.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `ed6f521df000904fb3769c03b382a285b361068f408d6448a4a28c4de5d18fd9`.

[examples/dopri5_eq1.f](https://github.com/cpmech/hwode/blob/784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3/examples/dopri5_eq1.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `a1a548ba62f9d460bf7d01d2bccd403b98c14c5770624d0c409630ce892ea6a8`.

Public entry point `DOPRI5`: [dopri5.f:1–350](https://github.com/cpmech/hwode/blob/784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3/dopri5.f#L1-L350).

External double-precision nonstiff ODE driver. FCN(N,X,Y,F,RPAR,IPAR) supplies derivatives. ITOL=0 uses scalar tolerances and ITOL=1 vectors. Y and X are advanced. With NRDENS dense components, the author allocates LWORK=8*N+5*NRDENS+21 and LIWORK=NRDENS+21.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DOPRI5(N, FCN, X, Y, XEND, RTOL, ATOL, ITOL, &
     SOLOUT, IOUT, DEBUG, WORK, LWORK, IWORK, LIWORK, RPAR, IPAR, IDID)
```

Argument declarations: [dopri5.f:1–4](https://github.com/cpmech/hwode/blob/784b80fe5ed02670bd9f17a73489de42652c38b3/dopri5.f#L1-L4).

```fortran
! Initialize X/Y/XEND, tolerances, arrays and matching FCN/SOLOUT callbacks.
work = 0.0d0

call dopri5(n,fcn,x,y,xend,rtol,atol,0,solout,iout,debug, &

if (idid < 0) error stop "DOPRI5 failed"
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use positive compatible tolerances and initialized callback parameters. IDID=1 reaches the endpoint; 2 means interrupted by SOLOUT. Negative codes describe input, step-budget, step-size and stiffness failures. The pinned example enables dense output; the fragment above disables it.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `6ee15e29d77cc6789e55df4ba452fa2addcd4ec5780ba73f1267a12776745258`.

**E2b — source-reviewed**

The inspected quadratic_shepard_2d wrapper creates local quadratic models for scattered planar points through alg660::qshep2. The reviewed core builds weighted least-squares systems, applies Givens rotations and solves for nodal quadratic coefficients. qs2val blends those local polynomials with compact-support modified Shepard weights, returning the stored value exactly at a node; qs2grd differentiates that weighted quotient. E2b is scattered multivariate interpolation, not gridded tensor-product interpolation. Only this 2D path is reviewed: the spherical, triangulation and 3D variants are not certified here. The wrapper fixes neighbor counts, uses default REAL and requires at least six equal-length samples. Duplicate/collinear configurations and unsupported query locations have status paths. Query methods assume successful construction and do not guard against unallocated data. No interpolation or gradient check was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `3beca3e84a5407cfcc35360bfe9538f151ddb3e0`.

```fortran
CALL mesh%create_mesh(x, y, f)
```

Type-bound default REAL value query at a planar point (px,py). Construct successfully first and check error_status after each query. If no nodal support covers the query, the core returns a NaN and the wrapper records code_outside_spanned; this is not a general extrapolator.

Usage:

```fortran
value = mesh%interpolate_point(px, py)
```

Argument declarations: [src/qshep2d.f90:140–143](https://github.com/arjenmarkus/interpolation2d3d/blob/3beca3e84a5407cfcc35360bfe9538f151ddb3e0/src/qshep2d.f90#L140-L143).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use quadratic_shepard_2d, only: qshep_2d
type(qshep_2d) :: mesh
real :: x(9), y(9), f(9), value
integer :: status
x = [0.,1.,2.,0.,1.,2.,0.,1.,2.]
y = [0.,0.,0.,1.,1.,1.,2.,2.,2.]
f = x+y
call mesh%create_mesh(x,y,f)
call mesh%error_status(status)
if (status /= 0) error stop "mesh creation failed"
value = mesh%interpolate_point(0.5,0.5)
call mesh%error_status(status)
if (status /= 0) error stop "query failed"
```

Uncompiled calling sketch using the pinned type and bindings. Compile interpolate_frame and alg660 before quadratic_shepard_2d. The affine expected value is 1, but neither this sketch nor the author randomized example was run. Error status is mutable per query; inspect it before another operation overwrites it.

Public entry point `quadratic_shepard_2d::qshep_2d%gradient_point`: [src/qshep2d.f90:185–227](https://github.com/arjenmarkus/interpolation2d3d/blob/3beca3e84a5407cfcc35360bfe9538f151ddb3e0/src/qshep2d.f90#L185-L227).

Returns a two-element default REAL vector of derivatives of the fitted interpolant with respect to px and py. It does not supply derivatives of an unknown sampled function. Check error_status; the unsupported-location branch returns zero components with a nonzero status.

```fortran
gradient = mesh%gradient_point(px, py)
```

THETA3 dispatches to a logarithmic implementation that shifts/inverts tau, reduces z, sums paired exponential terms and finally exponentiates the result. Source uses exp(i*pi*n*(tau*n+2*z)), so z has real period one, unlike conventions with period pi. Require Im(tau)>0. Invalid tau, excessive transformation/shift recursion and detected NaNs call EXIT(-1), terminating the process rather than returning status. MAXITER limits transformations/shifts, not the final series loop, whose stopping test uses floating-point stagnation. Only THETA3 and the inspected shared helper path are mapped here; the other advertised theta/log/generalized interfaces are not independently certified.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `ea49a80f47de5fde413d426521a2e970f8c682c1`.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected external newtonhook routine solves a square residual system using a matrix-vector callback, right-preconditioned GMRES and SVD-regularized hooksteps. It compares actual residual-norm reduction with the predicted reduction and retries trust-region radii. The author example approximates J*v by directional residual differences around module state new_x/new_fx; the core itself accepts a supplied operator and does not automatically differentiate an arbitrary callback. This is F2 root finding, not a general constrained optimizer or ODE integrator. Source limitations remain: newtonhook overwrites the GMRES return flag ginfo with the input print flag info immediately after the solve, so the advertised GMRES-failure propagation is not established; GMRES normalizes residual/Arnoldi vectors without explicit zero-norm guards. Some linear-algebra failures STOP. Reusing the saved Krylov state and module-wide solution arrays requires coordinated calls. No failure, periodic orbit or nonlinear accuracy result was reproduced.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `8d010109bc59958ff0d9cd83e4e6216a3de65a207cc18518e580afc1a128fa31`.

Public entry point `newtonhook`: [Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90:56–190](https://github.com/apwillis1/JFNK-Hookstep/blob/8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896/Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90#L56-L190).

External routine using the separate module newton for saved state. Allocate new_x(n), new_fx(n), set new_x to the initial guess, then provide f(n,x,y), df(n,v,jv), in-place preconditioner dfp(n,v), parameterless monitor sub(), and double-precision dp(n,a,b). df must apply the Jacobian at the current shared iterate. info is both print-control input and termination output. Tolerances and trust-radius parameters are double precision; del=0 disables hooksteps.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL newtonhook(f, df, dfp, sub, dp, m, n, gtol, tol, del, mndl, mxdl, nits, info)
```

Argument declarations: [Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90:60–65](https://github.com/apwillis1/JFNK-Hookstep/blob/8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896/Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90#L60-L65).

Argument declarations: [Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90:47–53](https://github.com/apwillis1/JFNK-Hookstep/blob/8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896/Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90#L47-L53).

Argument declarations: [Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90:24–44](https://github.com/apwillis1/JFNK-Hookstep/blob/8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896/Fortran90/NewtonHook.f90#L24-L44).

Author example (not run): [Fortran90/newton_Lorenz.f90:57–87](https://github.com/apwillis1/JFNK-Hookstep/blob/8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896/Fortran90/newton_Lorenz.f90#L57-L87).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use newton, only: new_x, new_fx
external :: newtonhook, residual, jacobian_action, precondition, monitor
double precision, external :: inner_product
integer :: info
allocate(new_x(2),new_fx(2))
new_x = [1.0d0,1.0d0]
info = 0
call newtonhook(residual,jacobian_action,precondition,monitor,inner_product, &
                2,2,1.0d-3,1.0d-8,1.0d0,1.0d-12,10.0d0,50,info)
! Check info and the independently evaluated residual at new_x.
```

Calling fragment only. Implement all callbacks; jacobian_action may use analytic products or the documented directional-difference template, precondition may be the identity and monitor may do nothing. Compile the source defining module newton before the caller and link GMRESm plus compatible LAPACK/BLAS. Choose m large enough for the Krylov solve; the author warns that restarting affects hookstep correctness. Module storage is shared. No system or claimed termination behavior was run.

Implementation evidence `gmresm`: [Fortran90/GMRESm.f90:35–123](https://github.com/apwillis1/JFNK-Hookstep/blob/8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896/Fortran90/GMRESm.f90#L35-L123).

Implementation evidence `hookstep`: [Fortran90/GMRESm.f90:130–161](https://github.com/apwillis1/JFNK-Hookstep/blob/8ae8c0d76e08dbbfa37258c45dd4a71406e0a896/Fortran90/GMRESm.f90#L130-L161).

**D6 — source-reviewed**

The real64 DKSVD0 interface and its included gksvd0 body implement a two-sided Kogbetliantz SVD of a square N-by-N matrix. The body generates index pairs, extracts 2-by-2 pivots, applies left/right rotations, optionally accumulates U and V, and extracts singular values from the transformed diagonal. D6 is already a GAMS leaf, with no separate cyclic or precision subclass. This review follows the cyclic/quasi-cyclic real64 path, not every blocked, dynamic, complex or higher-precision variant. Some strategies require even N. DKSVD2 is a Fortran wrapper around the external libpvn PVN_DLJSV2 kernel; it is not an independent local implementation of that 2-by-2 algorithm. INFO carries an input step budget/accuracy mode and an output sweep count or limit, rather than a universal zero-success convention. Scaling, rounding assumptions, reconstruction, orthogonality and parallel performance were not tested; no rectangular-matrix claim is inferred from the repository title.

External REAL64 square-matrix SVD subroutine. G is overwritten; SV holds the singular values and JOB controls the pivot strategy and initialization/accumulation of U and V. All leading dimensions, schedule/work arrays and INFO must be prepared explicitly. INFO is an input step budget (with sign-dependent mode) and an output status/sweep count, not solely a LAPACK-style output error code.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DKSVD0(JOB, N, G, LDG, U, LDU, V, LDV, SV, W, O, R, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [src/blksvd/dksvd0.F90:78–89](https://github.com/venovako/KogAcc/blob/c852e6d85355b5e7f3efb58b86cbe0c043cecd7d/src/blksvd/dksvd0.F90#L78-L89).

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected LBFGS path constructs a limited-memory inverse-Hessian action from stored step/gradient-difference pairs, uses a More-Thuente-style MCSRCH line search and requests function/gradient values through reverse communication. The user supplies first derivatives, not a Hessian; G1b1b records smooth multivariate unconstrained minimization. DIAGCO optionally requests a positive diagonal scaling through IFLAG=2. The normal stopping test is ||G||/max(1,||X||)<=EPS after a completed line search; no global-optimality or local-minimum certificate is implied. The initial step is 1/||G|| before that test, so an exactly stationary starting point is not safely handled by this path. LBFGS and MCSRCH retain SAVE state and shared LB3 parameters; do not interleave independent solves as though this interface were reentrant. Preserve workspace and re-enter with the returned IFLAG. No minimization, gradient comparison or full audit of MCSTEP/BLAS dependencies was executed.

Public entry point `LBFGS`: [lbfgs.f:8–428](https://github.com/jmbr/lbfgs/blob/dc92c88d19673093ea695d0b7fa3f99eb08e00b4/lbfgs.f#L8-L428).

External double-precision reverse-communication minimizer. N/M are positive default INTEGER; W needs N*(2*M+1)+2*M elements. Initially evaluate F/G and set IFLAG=0. Return 1 requests fresh F/G at X, 2 requests positive DIAG when DIAGCO is true, 0 reports normal completion and negative values report errors. Link the LB2 block-data defaults and keep the state/workspace intact between calls.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL LBFGS(N, M, X, F, G, DIAGCO, DIAG, IPRINT, EPS, XTOL, W, IFLAG)
```

Argument declarations: [lbfgs.f:8–13](https://github.com/jmbr/lbfgs/blob/dc92c88d19673093ea695d0b7fa3f99eb08e00b4/lbfgs.f#L8-L13).

Argument declarations: [lbfgs.f:126–167](https://github.com/jmbr/lbfgs/blob/dc92c88d19673093ea695d0b7fa3f99eb08e00b4/lbfgs.f#L126-L167).

Author example (not run): [sdrive.f:13–59](https://github.com/jmbr/lbfgs/blob/dc92c88d19673093ea695d0b7fa3f99eb08e00b4/sdrive.f#L13-L59).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: lbfgs, lb2
integer, parameter :: n=2, m=3
integer :: iprint(2), iflag, calls
double precision :: x(n), g(n), diag(n), w(n*(2*m+1)+2*m)
double precision :: f, eps, xtol
logical :: diagco
x=[2.0d0,-1.0d0]
diagco=.false.
iprint=[-1,0]
eps=1.0d-8
xtol=epsilon(1.0d0)
iflag=0
do calls=1,1000
  f=0.5d0*sum(x*x)
  g=x
  call lbfgs(n,m,x,f,g,diagco,diag,iprint,eps,xtol,w,iflag)
  if (iflag <= 0) exit
  if (iflag /= 1) error stop "unexpected reverse-communication request"
end do
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "L-BFGS did not finish normally"
```

Uncompiled fragment minimizing a quadratic from an explicitly nonstationary initial point. It uses DIAGCO=false, so no diagonal-request branch is needed. The 1000-call guard is a caller limit, not a library convergence claim. Check an initially stationary point before entering this implementation. Link the complete lbfgs.f object, including LB2 and bundled support routines, with compatible default INTEGER/double precision; archive/block-data retention may require toolchain-specific handling. Saved/shared state prevents safe interleaving of solves.

Implementation helper `MCSRCH`: [lbfgs.f:623–925](https://github.com/jmbr/lbfgs/blob/dc92c88d19673093ea695d0b7fa3f99eb08e00b4/lbfgs.f#L623-L925).

**G2h1a2 — source-reviewed**

SETULB partitions workspace and dispatches MAINLB. The inspected MAINLB path projects the initial point onto simple bounds, computes a generalized Cauchy point and subspace step, invokes line search and maintains limited-memory BFGS state. This is smooth simple-bound optimization with caller-supplied first derivatives, not general nonlinear constraints or a global optimum guarantee. Reverse communication returns FG requests for objective/gradient and NEW_X for an accepted iterate. Inspect the final TASK, including error and abnormal-termination strings. The review covers dispatch and iteration structure, not all linked kernels or numerical convergence.

External reverse-communication driver. NBD=0/1/2/3 means no/lower/both/upper bounds. Preserve all state arrays between calls. WA requires 2*M*N+5*N+11*M*M+8*M doubles; IWA(3*N), LSAVE(4), ISAVE(44), DSAVE(29), TASK and CSAVE of length 60 are required.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL SETULB(N, M, X, L, U, NBD, F, G, FACTR, PGTOL, WA, IWA, &
     TASK, IPRINT, CSAVE, LSAVE, ISAVE, DSAVE)
```

Argument declarations: [src/setulb.f:188–198](https://github.com/jonathanschilling/L-BFGS-B/blob/289d99c2981ce7852e8d2f0ddb8716289076947a/src/setulb.f#L188-L198).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
! Declare/allocate the documented workspace and initialize X, bounds and NBD.
task = "START"
do
  call setulb(n,m,x,l,u,nbd,f,g,factr,pgtol,wa,iwa, &
       task,iprint,csave,lsave,isave,dsave)
  if (task(1:2) == "FG") then
    ! Evaluate both F and G at the returned X here.
  else if (task(1:5) == "NEW_X") then
    cycle
  else
    exit
  end if
end do
! Inspect TASK; an exit is not necessarily convergence.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Fragment requires an objective, gradient, initialized tolerances and all library dependencies. FACTR scales a relative reduction tolerance by machine precision; PGTOL bounds the projected-gradient norm. Add an application evaluation/iteration budget. The linked author driver demonstrates reverse communication.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected 1D method selects a neighboring interval and evaluates a two-point affine formula, so the supported mapping is univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation (E1a), not arbitrary-degree global Lagrange interpolation inferred from the repository name. The public method creates/destroys private stored data per call and supports none/constant/linear extrapolation selectors. Important source findings remain: constant extrapolation returns endpoint x values rather than y values; early exits do not assign the optional success output; an unsorted-input create failure is not checked before using internal arrays; and normal cleanup resets the public object success property even after a successful optional status has been assigned. The naive method also uses adjacent-point linear interpolation. Author tests query supplied nodes rather than establishing between-node accuracy. No interpolation result or failure was reproduced by execution.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The 2D method applies the 1D adjacent-point interpolation along grid rows and then along the other axis. E2a records gridded bivariate interpolation, not scattered-data fitting, an arbitrary-degree polynomial or a mesh generator. The data layout read by source is fxy_data(size(x_data),size(y_data)). The final along-x interpolation is inside the row-filling loop, so early iterations read not-yet-filled x_estimate elements; although the final iteration has all entries filled, invalid-value traps or intermediate results were not investigated. There is no 2D status output and the 1D failure/extrapolation limitations propagate. Tests use an equal-sized grid and node queries; nonsquare grids and between-node behavior were not verified by execution.

**D2a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected DGESV driver solves a general real dense square system with one or more right-hand sides. It checks dimensions, dispatches LU factorization with partial pivoting to DGETRF and solves through DGETRS only if factorization reports success. A is overwritten by LU factors and B by the solution; positive INFO reports an exactly zero pivot. D2a1 is the general-system class. This source review covers the driver interface and dispatch, not an audit of every BLAS/LAPACK kernel or vendor implementation. It does not establish conditioning, error bounds, inverse formation, sparse support or numerical accuracy by execution.

External double-precision dense linear-system driver. A(LDA,N) is overwritten by factors, B(LDB,NRHS) by solutions, and IPIV(N) records row pivots. Check INFO before using the solution. Link a compatible LAPACK/BLAS library; this source file alone is insufficient.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DGESV(N, NRHS, A, LDA, IPIV, B, LDB, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [SRC/dgesv.f:121–133](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dgesv.f#L121-L133).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dgesv
integer :: ipiv(2), info
double precision :: a(2,2), b(2,1)
a = reshape([3.0d0, 1.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0], [2,2])
b(:,1) = [9.0d0, 8.0d0]
call dgesv(2, 1, a, 2, ipiv, b, 2, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGESV failed"
! The solution is now in b(:,1).
```

Calling sketch only, not a checked driver. Use a double-precision/integer ABI compatible with the linked LAPACK build; a vendor ILP64 build needs matching integer arguments. Preserve input copies if residuals or the original matrix are needed. INFO=0 is not a condition-number or accuracy estimate. No compilation, residual calculation or solver comparison was performed.

**D9a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected real DGELS driver chooses QR or LQ factorization by matrix shape and applies orthogonal transformations and triangular solves for unconstrained least squares or minimum-norm underdetermined solves. For TRANS=N and M>=N, the reviewed path forms Q-transpose B and solves with R. The interface assumes full rank; positive INFO detects exactly zero triangular diagonals, not reliable numerical rank or near-singularity. D9a1 records the unconstrained L2 solution scope. Workspace queries and scaling are visible in the driver. This review does not certify all dependency kernels, rank-deficient methods, constrained least squares or runtime accuracy.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce`.

[SRC/dgels.f](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dgels.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `1c0c4aa4314403dbe3641bda2f29013bfac55c72df2ca2651fe86d8160594901`.

Public entry point `DGELS`: [SRC/dgels.f:189–525](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dgels.f#L189-L525).

External full-rank real least-squares/minimum-norm driver. TRANS selects A or its transpose. A and B are overwritten; B needs at least MAX(1,M,N) rows even when the input right-hand side is shorter. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 before allocating the working buffer, then check INFO after the solve.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DGELS(TRANS, M, N, NRHS, A, LDA, B, LDB, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [SRC/dgels.f:189–203](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dgels.f#L189-L203).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dgels
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(3,2), b(3,1), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a(:,1) = 1.0d0
a(:,2) = [0.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0]
b(:,1) = [1.0d0, 2.0d0, 2.0d0]
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, work, lwork, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS failed"
! For this M>=N case, b(1:2,1) holds the fitted coefficients.
```

Calling sketch only. Link compatible LAPACK and BLAS and match the integer/real ABI. The example uses the full-rank overdetermined TRANS=N branch; it is not a rank-revealing solver demonstration. Preserve original A/B for an independent residual check. Neither the fit nor any underdetermined branch was run for this catalog.

**D4a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected DSYEV driver computes ordinary eigenvalues of a real symmetric dense matrix, optionally eigenvectors. It reads the selected triangle, reduces through DSYTRD and dispatches eigenvalues-only work to DSTERF or the vector path through DORGTR and DSTEQR; optional scaling is undone on the eigenvalues. D4a1 is the real-symmetric ordinary-eigenproblem scope. This is not a generalized, complex, nonsymmetric or subset-eigensolver mapping. The driver exposes workspace-query and convergence status, but no eigenpair residual, orthogonality check or audit of all lower-level kernels was performed.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce`.

[SRC/dsyev.f](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dsyev.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `9c9dcb34fed866f91ddd785897c653a94671fd75bc2856171b18547cb6fafe62`.

Public entry point `DSYEV`: [SRC/dsyev.f:129–281](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dsyev.f#L129-L281).

External double-precision symmetric eigensolver. JOBZ selects values alone or values plus vectors; UPLO selects the stored triangle. Eigenvalues are returned in ascending order. A is overwritten, holding eigenvectors on a successful JOBZ=V call. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 and check INFO.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL DSYEV(JOBZ, UPLO, N, A, LDA, W, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
```

Argument declarations: [SRC/dsyev.f:129–141](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/472b3a0fcbc5e90bf30a41b13ead24e40fff54ce/SRC/dsyev.f#L129-L141).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dsyev
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(2,2), w(2), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a = reshape([2.0d0, 1.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0], [2,2])
call dsyev("V", "U", 2, a, 2, w, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DSYEV query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))
call dsyev("V", "U", 2, a, 2, w, work, lwork, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DSYEV failed"
! w contains eigenvalues; columns of a contain eigenvectors.
```

Calling sketch only. Match the linked LAPACK/BLAS ABI and use only the selected triangle as input. Keep the original matrix for independent eigenpair-residual and orthogonality checks; INFO=0 alone is not such a check. Neither the sample eigenproblem nor the author test suite was run.

## Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto Quadrature

**License: GNU GPL version 3**

**H2a — documentation-reviewed**

The short README identifies the quadrature module and supporting polynomials. No particular order range, endpoint accuracy or asymptotic complexity is inferred without source review.

[README.md](https://github.com/SpirosZafeiris/Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto-Quadrature/blob/8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `177498effaa9724b33e8f4fd3e925e889e610873e25b4ff168f37061e896c919`.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

LGL_nodes_weights constructs a requested-size Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto rule on [-1,1], using endpoint nodes and Jacobi-root iterations for the interior. LGL_quadrature combines a caller-provided vector of values at those nodes with the weights and scales by (b-a)/2. H2a1b2 describes this nonautomatic sampled-data finite-interval quadrature: the caller chooses N and supplies values; there is no integrand callback, adaptive subdivision, requested-accuracy controller or estimated-error return. The values must correspond to the mapped LGL nodes, not arbitrary or uniformly spaced samples. Jacobi-root iterations stop after at most ten steps with no convergence status, and small-N and high-order behavior were not verified. The pinned source also uses triplet-style array constructors such as [size_r:1:-1], requiring compiler support or source adaptation; no portable-build claim is made. General Jacobi/Gauss routines, polynomial exactness claims and author example results remain unverified by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260`.


Calling sketch only. Resolve the pinned source array-constructor syntax for your compiler first. Nodes are on [-1,1]; map them to the physical interval before sampling the integrand. The fixed iteration cap supplies no convergence flag, so this sketch is not a checked quadrature rule.

Public entry point `legendre_gauss_lobatto::LGL_quadrature`: [lgl.f90:80–90](https://github.com/SpirosZafeiris/Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto-Quadrature/blob/8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260/lgl.f90#L80-L90).

Public module reduction function for N values sampled at the LGL nodes mapped onto [a,b]. f(N), a, b and the scalar result are REAL(wp). The routine regenerates its rule internally and supplies no estimated error or status output.

Usage:

```fortran
integral = LGL_quadrature(N, f, a, b)
```

Argument declarations: [lgl.f90:80–85](https://github.com/SpirosZafeiris/Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto-Quadrature/blob/8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260/lgl.f90#L80-L85).

Author example (not run): [main.f90:16–26](https://github.com/SpirosZafeiris/Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto-Quadrature/blob/8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260/main.f90#L16-L26).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use legendre_gauss_lobatto, only: wp, LGL_nodes_weights, LGL_quadrature
integer, parameter :: n = 6
real(wp) :: rule(n,2), x(n), values(n), a, b, integral
a = -1.0_wp
b = 2.0_wp
rule = LGL_nodes_weights(n)
x = a + 0.5_wp*(b-a)*(rule(:,1)+1.0_wp)
values = exp(x)
integral = LGL_quadrature(n, values, a, b)
```

Calling sketch adapted to the author exponential-integral example, not a checked driver. The source uses compiler-dependent triplet-style constructors; resolve that before compiling. N is an explicit rule size, not an error tolerance, and there is no accuracy/status result. The integrand must be sampled at the rule nodes in the returned order.

Implementation helper `legendre_gauss_lobatto::jacpts / jacpts_main`: [lgl.f90:151–207](https://github.com/SpirosZafeiris/Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto-Quadrature/blob/8ff674ed77eff6ed7e0c1b58755a182c4a5e1260/lgl.f90#L151-L207).

**C12 — source-reviewed**

The public COUL90 module procedure is defined in a submodule, despite introductory wrapper prose calling it complex. The inspected KFN=0 path uses real64 X/ETA/order inputs, computes continued fractions with a 20000-iteration cap, recurs across integer-spaced real orders and normalizes regular/irregular Coulomb functions and x derivatives. JWKB is dispatched near the turning region; that helper is not independently audited. Arrays are written beginning at MINL=MAX(INT(XLMIN+ACCUR),0), ending MINL+LRANGE, so size depends on the base order rather than LRANGE alone. Require X>1e-7 (the square root of fixed ACCUR=1e-14), XLMIN>-1 and LRANGE>=0. Check IFAIL; fixed target accuracy and module diagnostic state do not establish a numerical error guarantee or reentrancy. Bessel/wrapper APIs are outside this mapping.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `5f7190432e0baa6a3ae9369e1c0ef5371b3f888d`.

Public module subroutine taking real64 scalars and four assumed-shape output arrays with dummy lower bound zero. KFN=0 selects Coulomb F/G and derivatives; LRANGE is the number of additional orders. Allocate every array to include indices MINL through MINL+LRANGE and inspect IFAIL before use.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL coul90(X, ETA_IN, XLMIN, LRANGE, FC, GC, FCP, GCP, KFN, IFAIL)
```

Argument declarations: [src/libcoul90.f:26–40](https://github.com/banana-bred/libcoul90/blob/5f7190432e0baa6a3ae9369e1c0ef5371b3f888d/src/libcoul90.f#L26-L40).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use libcoul90, only: coul90
real(real64) :: f(0:0),g(0:0),fp(0:0),gp(0:0)
integer :: status
call coul90(1.0_real64,0.0_real64,0.0_real64,0,f,g,fp,gp,0,status)
if (status /= 0) error stop "COUL90 failed"
! Zero-eta/order-zero reference: F=sin(1), G=cos(1).
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The analytic comparison is suggested, not executed. IFAIL=-1 reports small/negative X, -2 inconsistent orders, 1/2 continued-fraction limits. Compile parent module, defining submodule and support modules together. Shared diagnostic modules replace legacy COMMON state; do not assume independent concurrent invocations. No wrapper default, Bessel behavior or full helper/kernel accuracy was checked.

**E3a2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected SPLDER routine differences B-spline coefficients recursively to obtain derivative coefficients, then evaluates the lower-degree basis with FPBSPL; the highest derivative has a piecewise-constant branch. This is derivative evaluation of a supplied spline, not numerical differentiation of an arbitrary callback or recovery of derivatives of an unknown sampled function. The caller supplies knots, coefficients and spline degree. The fixed work arrays support the FITPACK degree range through five. The input checks cover derivative order and sorted queries, not complete knot validity or coefficient construction. The nonconstant branch clamps out-of-range queries to endpoints, while the highest-derivative branch differs; keep queries in the documented spline interval. No spline value, derivative or author example was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `5dd7bd76738153e4cda2a0269e2bdfd6b386976d`.

External default REAL routine for an existing normalized B-spline representation. Provide t(n), c(n), sorted x(m), y(m), wrk(n), 1 <= k <= 5 and 0 <= nu <= k, with valid knots. Keep query points in [t(k+1),t(n-k)]. Check ier before using y: zero is normal return, ten reports some invalid inputs.

```fortran
CALL splder(t, n, c, k, nu, x, y, m, wrk, ier)
```

**E3a3 — source-reviewed**

SPLINT obtains integrals of the normalized B-spline basis from FPINTB and contracts them with the supplied spline coefficients. The helper uses the Gaffney recurrence, reverses sign for reversed integration limits and clips limits to the spline support. E3a3 records quadrature of an already-fitted function, rather than an adaptive integrator for arbitrary functions. The spline is treated as zero outside its base interval according to the public header. The routine has no status or error estimate and assumes valid knots, degree and storage. The helper contains six-element local arrays, consistent with degree at most five; it is not a general arbitrary-degree API. No integral or author example was checked by execution.

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The inspected STEEPEST_DESCENT entry uses a user objective and array-valued gradient, normalizes the descent direction, dispatches quadratic line interpolation with golden-section fallback, and tests mean squared gradient and relative cost change. Only this local smooth supplied-gradient method is mapped here, not the unreviewed CG/BFGS entries in the same file. Source findings: normalization precedes the zero-gradient test, relative cost change divides by the previous cost, and a SAVE allocatable gradient is allocated only once without resizing. Stationary points, zero costs, changing dimensions and reentrancy therefore require attention before relying on this implementation.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `747a81b7a022210ae780314bbc5e25e21e9036c2`.

[minimize.F90](https://github.com/ryokbys/minimize/blob/747a81b7a022210ae780314bbc5e25e21e9036c2/minimize.F90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `3d03393396677b4441677397e1d040d80e83c407765d0d736b5d8f9beaac9858`.

Public entry point `steepest_descent`: [minimize.F90:2–92](https://github.com/ryokbys/minimize/blob/747a81b7a022210ae780314bbc5e25e21e9036c2/minimize.F90#L2-L92).

External REAL(8) minimizer. FUNC(N,X) returns a scalar; GRAD(N,X) returns an N-vector. X/F and IFLAG are input/output. Initialize IFLAG=0 and inspect arithmetic status additions, rather than treating every return as success. REAL(8) is the author kind choice, not a portable real64 declaration.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL steepest_descent(NDIM, X, F, XTOL, GTOL, FTOL, MAXITER, &
     IPRINT, IFLAG, FUNC, GRAD)
```

Argument declarations: [minimize.F90:2–21](https://github.com/ryokbys/minimize/blob/747a81b7a022210ae780314bbc5e25e21e9036c2/minimize.F90#L2-L21).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
! Declare matching scalar FUNC and array-valued GRAD callbacks and REAL(8) inputs.
iflag = 0
call steepest_descent(ndim,x,f,xtol,gtol,ftol,maxiter, &
     0,iflag,func,grad)
! Decode IFLAG and independently check the returned point.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. An explicit matching interface is needed for the array-valued gradient. This calling fragment does not repair zero-gradient/zero-cost divisions or saved-array resizing. GTOL is compared with SUM(G**2)/NDIM; convergence diagnostics can still print at IPRINT=0. No runtime failure or convergence was reproduced.

**G2h3 — source-reviewed**

The main program minimizes x(n), the common ball radius, through an external bmalgencan::algencan call. evalc computes the uncovered-area constraint as total polygon area minus covered area, while evalg, evalj and evalhl supply objective gradient, geometric constraint derivatives and sparse Lagrangian-Hessian entries. The objective Hessian is explicitly zero. This establishes a specialized nonlinear constrained optimization implementation (G2h3), not a generic optimizer implemented in this repository. A smoothness-specific leaf is withheld: the geometry includes tolerances, deterministic small center perturbations, topology changes and zero-derivative fallbacks for invalid configurations. Merely exposing derivative callbacks does not establish a global C2 contract; a later review must also resolve the external solver constraint convention before selecting the equality/inequality branch. The Makefile requires external ALGENCAN 4, HSL and BLAS; its single driver and restart/initialization heuristics do not certify a global minimum. No solve, derivative formula or asymptotic bound was verified.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `f97119df01ae48e396f881ad2d2e25085338282b`.

**P — source-reviewed**

The VorCells_Polygons module exposes Voronoi-cell/polygon intersections and convex-polygon/circle intersections used by the area constraint. VorCellInterConvPol dispatches to a Sutherland-Hodgman half-plane clipping implementation; edgeClipping classifies edges with visibility tests and constructs intersections. interCellBall combines segment-circle intersections with polygon vertices and curved-edge identifiers. This source review strengthens the existing P documentation mapping: P itself is a GAMS leaf, so no invented polygon/Voronoi subclasses are introduced. Private clipping helpers are recorded as implementation evidence, not claimed as public APIs. The module delegates geometric primitives to bundled GEOMETRY/GEOMPACK routines; those entire inherited libraries are not audited here. Tolerance-sensitive degeneracies, collinear paths and exact-predicate robustness remain unverified. No clipping, area or coverage driver was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `f97119df01ae48e396f881ad2d2e25085338282b`.

External double-precision square-system solver, also declared by module minpack. X(N) is input initial guess/output solution; FVEC(N) residual, WA length at least N*(3*N+13)/2. Default INTEGER dimensions/status. Check INFO and residuals. Callback FCN(N,X,FVEC,IFLAG) supplies values; no user Jacobian.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL hybrd1(fcn, n, x, fvec, tol, info, wa, lwa)
```

**K1b1a2 — source-reviewed**

LMDER1 configures LMDER for unconstrained nonlinear L2 least squares with supplied residual Jacobian, M>=N, relative cost/step tolerances and evaluation budget 100*(N+1). The inspected driver uses pivoted QR and Levenberg-Marquardt parameter/step dispatch. K1b1a2 records smooth unconstrained nonlinear least squares with user first derivatives, not arbitrary-objective optimization, bounds or rank-certified parameter identification. INFO=1..4 describe different normal stopping tests, not a zero-residual guarantee. The repository module callback interface declares IFLAG INTENT(IN) and both residual/Jacobian INTENT(OUT), conflicting with the classic preserve-the-unused-array/abort contract. The sketch uses the external routine and requires a correctly declared callback. No fit or Jacobian was checked and subordinate linear algebra is not audited.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `12f30bc2d6971fde7a32d59e80c635289376e14a`.

**C19 — source-reviewed**

The public MLF_GARRAPPA generic maps scalar/rank-1/rank-2/rank-3 inputs to private bindings. The inspected scalar two-parameter binding sets gamma=1 and dispatches SUB_GENMLF_MULTISHOT: alpha=beta=1 returns EXP, tiny z uses reciprocal Gamma(beta), and other cases dispatch inverse-Laplace evaluation with contour-parameter selection and residue contributions. The source review covers scalar entry/dispatch and contour evaluation structure, not every parameter-optimization, Gamma or sorting helper. Alpha must be positive. Invalid parameters print diagnostics and return without reliably defined outputs or a status code. The saved epsilon and RNG initialization are shared side effects. This is not a review of the separate derivative generic or all generalized three-parameter domains.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `54195cb599c9f5018a9fc912dc3fb31f5dfb2800`.

**C1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected public BINOMIALCOEF returns individual binomial coefficients as REAL64, using a stored Pascal table through n=20 and BINOMIALCOEFSARRAY Pascal recurrence above that. The array routine reconstructs each row from the previous row with endpoint ones. This is the GAMS integer-valued combinatorial-function scope, although the representation is floating point rather than exact arbitrary-size integers. For n>=0, out-of-range j returns zero. Negative n is not a supported validated input and large coefficients lose exactness or overflow; the routines return no status. Other utility modules and the separate table-generating API are not promoted by this source review.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `67b44438ba62009182e22f81a060273e25fcfabf`.

**J1a2 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed FFTpack type exposes public fft/ifft generics for in-place one-dimensional complex transforms. Each method determines N from the array, destroys/reallocates workspace, initializes factors/twiddle tables through CFFT1I, calls CFFT1F or CFFT1B and destroys workspace again. It is not a cached-plan interface. The low-level forward path reinterprets complex storage through ISO_C_BINDING and dispatches radix passes; the inspected terminal radix-four case scales by 1/(4*l1), consistent with the documented forward-normalized/inverse-unscaled convention. This differs from FFTE/FFTW-wrapper forward-unscaled conventions. J1a2 records complex 1D transforms, not all real, multidimensional or trigonometric variants. Supply a nonempty vector; workspace sizing uses log(N) and does not validate N>0 first. Errors may ERROR STOP instead of returning to the caller. Parent/submodule CFFT1F declarations differ in workspace INTENT attributes; compiler acceptance was not checked. Source review covers the wrapper, setup/dispatch and a normalization path, not all factorization/radix arithmetic, build portability or round-trip accuracy. No transform or author test was executed.

**H2a1a1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected legacy DQAG entry checks workspace and dispatches DQAGE, which selects a Gauss-Kronrod rule, estimates integral/error, bisects the largest-error subinterval and maintains error ordering through DQPSRT. Termination compares summed estimated error with max(EPSABS,EPSREL*abs(result)); IER reports tolerance, subdivision, roundoff or integrand difficulties. H2a1a1 covers automatic finite-interval callback quadrature. An error estimate is not a rigorous bound and oscillatory/singular/discontinuous functions need appropriate handling. This is the bundled double-precision legacy entry, not the unfinished high-level quadrature API. Review covers control flow and rule dispatch, not every kernel or machine-constant/error-handler implementation. No integral was evaluated.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `a736ad7813da21ca55e31d75415359379cf6be011ddb0bd65d679d8d70fa95c6`.

**G2i — source-reviewed**

The multiobjective DIRECT path keeps vector objective values and nondominated-point sets, evaluates rectangle centers and selects/subdivides rectangles. G2i is used for this global nonconvex search, with the multiobjective/Pareto scope explicit; the taxonomy supplies no separate multiobjective child here. The wrapper can combine MODIRECT and DFMO through separately budgeted phases. Crucially, the pinned CODE/main.f90 sets maxnf_MODIR=0, so the supplied main skips the global phase unless edited; this mapping describes an implemented optional path, not the default execution. Bounds and inequality-value callbacks are documented; no equality interface or complete Pareto-front guarantee is claimed. No phase was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `3896605a13c7467f15052e150621d44d55e3fc0d`.

Public entry point `wrapper`: [CODE/subroutines_RACCORDO.f90:29–40](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/MODIR/blob/3896605a13c7467f15052e150621d44d55e3fc0d/CODE/subroutines_RACCORDO.f90#L29-L40).

External high-level driver wrapper for MODIR/DFMO. Its two default-integer arguments are separate function-evaluation budgets. It obtains problem dimensions, bounds, objectives and inequalities from linked routines, manages shared solver state, and writes nondominated solutions to out_nondom.txt rather than returning a solution array.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL wrapper(maxnf_MODIR, maxnf_DFMO)
```

Argument declarations: [CODE/subroutines_RACCORDO.f90:73–84](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/MODIR/blob/3896605a13c7467f15052e150621d44d55e3fc0d/CODE/subroutines_RACCORDO.f90#L73-L84).

Author example (not run): [CODE/main.f90:1–14](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/MODIR/blob/3896605a13c7467f15052e150621d44d55e3fc0d/CODE/main.f90#L1-L14).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
! Link the upstream modules and your problem.f90 definitions.
! Choose budgets explicitly; enable MODIR with a positive budget.
maxnf_MODIR = 500*n
maxnf_DFMO = 0
call wrapper(maxnf_MODIR, maxnf_DFMO)
```

Calling sketch only; initialize n with the problem dimension before choosing budgets. The supplied main sets maxnf_MODIR=0, so running it unchanged does not exercise the global MODIR phase. Follow the README problem interfaces and upstream build/configuration files. main_MODIRECT is a lower-level phase routine requiring shared state and an initialized partition structure; it is retained as implementation evidence rather than recommended as the first call. No Pareto-front or execution check was performed here.

Implementation helper `main_MODIRECT`: [CODE/main_MODIRECT.f90:1–154](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/MODIR/blob/3896605a13c7467f15052e150621d44d55e3fc0d/CODE/main_MODIRECT.f90#L1-L154).

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The inspected spline object constructs tensor-product B-spline coefficients on Cartesian-product axes by solving one-dimensional basis systems successively, then evaluates target grids via basis matrices and BLAS products. Cox-de Boor recursion implements the basis, and the author 2D example concatenates x/y axes and flattens f(i,j) in Fortran order. This establishes gridded multivariate interpolation E2a, not scattered-data fitting. The basis order k means degree k-1 (k=4 is cubic). Supply valid strictly increasing axes and compatible sizes/orders. DGESV info is ignored in set_coefs_1d, so singular/invalid interpolation systems are not reported to the caller. Extrapolation is a saved module-wide flag shared across objects, not an object-specific setting; omitted init arguments retain its previous value. Reinitialization requires cleanup, and fin assumes initialized allocations. This review excludes skip_solve-only workflows and does not establish interpolation accuracy, extrapolation safety or derivative APIs. No author test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `c4b80d48764199708196b89ba046d50526bf2a9d`.

Public type-bound generic initializer for type(spline). ks(:) gives B-spline orders and ns(:) gives axis sizes; xs concatenates axes with length SUM(ns), and fs flattens the source grid with length PRODUCT(ns), first axis varying fastest. Use real64 arrays, at least two axes for this mapped scope, 1 <= ks <= ns, and valid distinct increasing axis coordinates. Set extrapolation explicitly; keep skip_solve false when evaluating data. Failures may STOP and no status is returned.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL sp%init(ks, ns, xs, fs, extrapolation, skip_solve)
```

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected unbounded newspline path constructs interval-wall control points, solves a linear system for mid-control adjustments using integrated Hermite basis formulas, then evaluates cubic Hermite pieces at subinterval sample locations. This supports univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation from interval means (E1a), not ordinary interpolation through point-valued samples. The construction targets continuous interval-mean constraints; exact equality of discrete output arithmetic means was not established. Boundary inputs act as adjacent buffer interval values in the wall/control formulas. Require at least two input intervals, matching positive subdivision counts and output storage of sum(nk). No size/status checks or recoverable solve flag are supplied. matsol substitutes a tiny value for a zero pivot and does not return conditioning information. Optional lower/upper/absolute/percentage adjustment branches are present but outside this unbounded-path review; their bounds and conservation are not certified. No mean-preservation or spline test was run.

**F2 — source-reviewed**

The reviewed NITSOL path solves a square residual system with inexact Newton steps and residual-norm backtracking. The public driver validates option selections, partitions caller workspace and dispatches to nitdrv. The inspected GMRES path uses Jacobian-vector products, modified Gram-Schmidt and Krylov corrections; nitjv chooses supplied analytic products or directional finite differences and optional right preconditioning. nitbt evaluates trial residuals and reduces the step until its decrease condition holds. F2 is the system-of-equations leaf; the internal linear solves and residual norms do not make this a general nonlinear least-squares or optimization API. BiCGSTAB/TFQMR dispatch is present, but those implementations were not reviewed. Normal termination also permits a small-step criterion without the residual reaching ftol, so independently check the returned residual. Common blocks, saved initialization and the block-data defaults require coordinated builds and do not establish thread safety. No nonlinear solve or convergence test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569`.
