Public entry point `nitsol`: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:1–604](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L1-L604).

External double-precision square-system solver. x(n) is the initial guess and returned iterate; f(n,xcur,fcur,rpar,ipar,itrmf) supplies the residual. jacv supplies selected J*v or right-preconditioner actions, or may be a dummy when both are disabled. Initialize the ten-element input array, provide info(6), parameter arrays and method-sized rwork, plus BLAS-compatible dot/norm callbacks. iterm=0 may mean small step rather than small residual; rwork(1:n) holds the final residual on the normal driver path.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL nitsol(n, x, f, jacv, ftol, stptol, input, info, rwork, rpar, ipar, iterm, dinpr, dnorm)
```

Argument declarations: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:4–9](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L4-L9).

Argument declarations: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:42–80](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L42-L80).

Argument declarations: [Nitsol/nitsol.f:92–106](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitsol.f#L92-L106).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: nitsol, residual, jacobian_action
double precision, external :: ddot, dnrm2
integer, parameter :: n=2, kd=2
integer :: options(10), info(6), ipar(1), iterm
double precision :: x(n), work(n*(kd+5)+kd*(kd+3)), rpar(1)
options = 0
options(4) = kd
x = [1.0d0,1.0d0]
rpar = 0.0d0
ipar = 0
call nitsol(n,x,residual,jacobian_action,1.0d-8,1.0d-10, &
            options,info,work,rpar,ipar,iterm,ddot,dnrm2)
! Check iterm and independently inspect work(1:n).
```

Uncompiled calling fragment for finite-difference, unpreconditioned GMRES. Supply an explicit residual implementation matching the documented callback and a linkable dummy jacobian_action (unused in these options). Link the complete NITSOL package including nitbd block data, required BLAS/LAPACK support and matching integer/double-precision ABI. GMRES workspace is n*(kd+5)+kd*(kd+3); different methods require different storage. No solution, residual or performance comparison was computed.

Implementation helper `nitdrv`: [Nitsol/nitdrv.f:487–644](https://github.com/cmacmackin/nitsol/blob/32b2432bb3c9180fa3ac5f9183033c2778963569/Nitsol/nitdrv.f#L487-L644).

**D9b1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected solve routine forms A-transpose A and A-transpose b, adds variables to a passive set according to the positive projected residual, solves passive normal equations through update_s/DSYSV, and moves toward feasible nonnegative coefficients before updating the residual. This supports constrained L2 least squares D9b1, specifically nonnegative coefficients, not general equality/inequality constraints or a rank-revealing QR method. The code overwrites X from zero and returns ||A X-b||. Material discrepancies: implementation sets MODE=1 and leaves it there on normal completion despite comments/README saying zero; -1 reports iteration exhaustion and returns infinite X/residual. The iteration counter advances only in the inner feasibility loop, so MAXITER is not a strict cap on all outer iterations or linear solves. update_s ignores INFO from both DSYSV workspace query and solve, so rank-deficient/singular normal equations have no safe reported fallback. Normal equations can amplify conditioning issues. No KKT, residual, rank-deficient case or execution was checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `a38ea00228d1d8d9ac78fac7cdf0903af253a48b`.

Public entry point `nnls::solve`: [nnls.f:85–175](https://github.com/cuamll/nnls/blob/a38ea00228d1d8d9ac78fac7cdf0903af253a48b/nnls.f#L85-L175).

Public module subroutine, also BIND(C,name="solve"). Fortran callers use module nnls. A(m,n), b(m), x(n), tolerance/residual use C_DOUBLE; dimension/mode/MAXITER scalars use C_INT. The binding lacks VALUE, so C scalar arguments are pointers. There are no INTENT declarations; pass variables rather than relying on input-only dummy semantics. A/b are not assigned in the inspected body; x is overwritten. Actual normal MODE is 1, not the documented 0.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL solve(A, b, x, m, n, mode, res, maxiter, tol)
```

Argument declarations: [nnls.f:85–95](https://github.com/cuamll/nnls/blob/a38ea00228d1d8d9ac78fac7cdf0903af253a48b/nnls.f#L85-L95).

Argument declarations: [nnls.f:9–17](https://github.com/cuamll/nnls/blob/a38ea00228d1d8d9ac78fac7cdf0903af253a48b/nnls.f#L9-L17).

Author example (not run): [main.f:22–36](https://github.com/cuamll/nnls/blob/a38ea00228d1d8d9ac78fac7cdf0903af253a48b/main.f#L22-L36).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use iso_c_binding, only: c_double, c_int
use nnls, only: solve
integer(c_int) :: m, n, mode, maxiter
real(c_double) :: a(3,2), b(3), x(2), res, tol
m=3_c_int
n=2_c_int
maxiter=100_c_int
tol=1.0e-10_c_double
a(:,1)=[1.0_c_double,0.0_c_double,0.0_c_double]
a(:,2)=[0.0_c_double,1.0_c_double,0.0_c_double]
b=[-1.0_c_double,2.0_c_double,1.0_c_double]
call solve(a,b,x,m,n,mode,res,maxiter,tol)
if (mode /= 1_c_int) error stop "NNLS did not finish normally"
```

Uncompiled fragment for a full-column-rank example with expected x=[0,2] and residual sqrt(2); neither result was checked. A nonzero least-squares residual can be the correct constrained optimum. Independently check finite outputs, feasibility and first-order optimality; MODE=1 alone does not establish those checks, especially because DSYSV status is ignored. Link compatible BLAS/LAPACK; C_INT must match the linked LAPACK integer ABI. The source is free-form despite its .f filename (upstream Makefile supplies that option).

Implementation evidence `nnls::update_s`: [nnls.f:31–76](https://github.com/cuamll/nnls/blob/a38ea00228d1d8d9ac78fac7cdf0903af253a48b/nnls.f#L31-L76).

Passive-set normal-equation helper. It is public but is not presented as a separate recommended user solve interface; DSYSV INFO is unchecked.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

CSPLREP constructs piecewise-cubic coefficients by solving a tridiagonal system for second derivatives with user-supplied endpoint curvatures; CSPLEV selects an interval and evaluates its local polynomial. Zero endpoint curvatures give a natural cubic spline. Require at least four matching sorted, well-separated data nodes. Source findings: fewer nodes return uninitialized coefficients, CSPLREP uses ALLOCATED(CSP%X).AND.SIZE(CSP%X) without guaranteed short-circuit evaluation, and the interval lookup can return 0 or N for outside/upper-end queries although coefficients have N-1 columns. Those queries are not safe extrapolation. The mapping covers fitting and scalar value evaluation, not derivative/integral/root helpers or a full dependency audit.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `65ee8b75b22ad300b54c87d632b3ebcd87de4b7c`.

**H1 — source-reviewed**

The inspected FDM path forms central first differences with step 1e-6, diagonal second differences with step 1e-3, and mixed Hessian entries from simultaneous positive/negative perturbations after subtracting diagonal contributions. LIBRARY_REAL8::DIFF selects this path when GLOBAL::GRAD_PAR=1 and initializes gradient/Hessian outputs. The objective is not a passed callback: OBJ_FUNC dispatches fixed selectors 1 (x cubed), 2 (sine plus cosine with degree-to-radian conversion), or 3 (von Mises stress with additional GLOBAL dimension setup). A new objective requires adapting the included source consistently across the typed modules. H1 is the differentiation leaf; the review establishes finite-difference implementation structure, not derivative accuracy. The supplied main selects a different hyper-dual path, which is not audited here, and complex/hyper-dual algorithm correctness is not inferred from the README. Unsupported method selection leaves zero outputs and unsupported objective selection leaves ANS unassigned. No error/status or user step-size parameter is exposed. No driver was compiled or run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `5a1c668f44433957e9c1029d471dbd66b914e87c`.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

The inspected DGAUSS routine constructs an n-point Gaussian rule from the monic orthogonal-polynomial recurrence coefficients. It builds the symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix implicitly, iterates eigenvalues and first eigenvector components, sorts nodes and scales squared components by dbeta(1), the measure mass. It returns nodes and weights rather than invoking an integrand or returning an integral. H2c is therefore the precise quadrature-service mapping; an internal eigensolver does not make this a general eigensystem API. The caller must supply a valid positive integration measure and consistent recurrence coefficients. Negative beta entries and iteration exhaustion have error returns; eps is an eigensolver convergence parameter, not a requested integration-error bound. Other ORTHPOL recurrence-generation and Gauss-Radau/Lobatto routines are outside this source review. No moment or quadrature test was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `07aee9bd398887c0f47ae5406b3be865aa692d40`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `cef2d1cc1bcbd910050c5ec5283b3a20c5073eee372aad8372be5c2b20fe0502`.

Public entry point `dgauss`: [legacy/dgauss.f:3–103](https://github.com/ivan-pi/orthpol/blob/07aee9bd398887c0f47ae5406b3be865aa692d40/legacy/dgauss.f#L3-L103).

External double-precision Gaussian-rule constructor. dalpha(n), dbeta(n), dzero(n), dweigh(n), and workspace de(n) are required. dbeta(1) is the total mass; later entries are recurrence coefficients. Supply n >= 1 and positive deps. ierr=0 indicates normal return; -1/-2 flag size/negative beta and a positive value flags iteration exhaustion. Form the weighted sum yourself.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL dgauss(n, dalpha, dbeta, deps, dzero, dweigh, ierr, de)
```

Argument declarations: [legacy/dgauss.f:3–9](https://github.com/ivan-pi/orthpol/blob/07aee9bd398887c0f47ae5406b3be865aa692d40/legacy/dgauss.f#L3-L9).

Argument declarations: [legacy/gauss.f:24–44](https://github.com/ivan-pi/orthpol/blob/07aee9bd398887c0f47ae5406b3be865aa692d40/legacy/gauss.f#L24-L44).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: dgauss
integer, parameter :: n=4
integer :: i, ierr
double precision :: alpha(n), beta(n), nodes(n), weights(n), work(n), q
alpha = 0.0d0
beta(1) = 2.0d0
do i=2,n
  beta(i) = dble(i-1)**2/(4.0d0*dble(i-1)**2-1.0d0)
end do
call dgauss(n,alpha,beta,epsilon(1.0d0),nodes,weights,ierr,work)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop "Gaussian rule failed"
q = sum(weights*nodes**6)
```

Uncompiled calling sketch using the monic Legendre recurrence on [-1,1]. The analytic integral of x**6 is 2/7, but no moment comparison was run. The measure weight is already represented by the recurrence and quadrature weights: do not multiply it into the sampled integrand again. Rule-generation convergence does not bound integration error for a general function.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

**K4 — source-reviewed**

The public ACPADE path (SOLVER=0) forms a Beach rational-approximation matrix with N=2*r coefficients, solves it in a least-squares sense and evaluates numerator degree r-1 over a monic degree-r denominator. This is rational/Padé approximation from sampled complex values, not a verified recovery of analytic continuation or guaranteed pole accuracy. The inspected scope uses NPRECISION=64 and MTR=0, dispatching standard ZGELS through double conversion; quad and SVD branches are not numerically audited. SOLVER=1 (Thiele) is explicitly unimplemented and STOPs. Even positive N, matched shapes, enough samples and a nonzero denominator are caller requirements. The low-level entry avoids reading pade.par but writes diagnostics to unit 90; the module also needs a generated gitversion include. Backend positive INFO can produce a log message and still return coefficients without a caller status.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `1a1139ff845e73ed4978d99907dc9fe9aef6c820`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `777bc715b2ede1511cc9fc465d1929335f5c3c87a3ffc9c9fb195ab47076575b`.

**E1b — source-reviewed**

poly_interp implements a Neville-style Lagrange correction recurrence for the polynomial through n+1 distinct samples, also propagating derivative corrections. It evaluates at zero, so callers shift their abscissae by the desired query. This is a single polynomial (E1b), distinct from the local moving-stencil grid wrapper. Output y(0) is the value and y(k) is derivative k, not divided Taylor coefficients. dy is the last signed interpolation correction, not a certified error bound. There is no input-validation/status interface; duplicate nodes divide by zero. Restrict this reviewed use to n >= 1 and 0 <= nd <= n: for n=0 or derivative orders beyond n, some dy entries need not be assigned. Accuracy, conditioning and behavior on closely spaced nodes were not checked by execution.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `5147f4797ce8f7278bcc34e8b1147f45e5283357`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `4241abda9bdbb59b8e60e9ff707bd4dd2bfb51f894aada3e9ccf8121c8c1e808`.

Public entry point `poly_interp`: [poly_interp.f90:11–113](https://github.com/jlm785/polynomial_interpolation/blob/5147f4797ce8f7278bcc34e8b1147f45e5283357/poly_interp.f90#L11-L113).

External routine using selected_real_kind(12), named REAL64 locally. Pass xin(0:n), yin(0:n), output y(0:nd), dy(0:nd), degree n >= 1 and derivative limit 0 <= nd <= n. xin must contain distinct offsets from the target point, not absolute nodes unless querying zero. No error status is returned. dy entries are signed corrections, not guaranteed absolute errors.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL poly_interp(y, dy, xin, yin, n, nd)
```

Argument declarations: [poly_interp.f90:15–27](https://github.com/jlm785/polynomial_interpolation/blob/5147f4797ce8f7278bcc34e8b1147f45e5283357/poly_interp.f90#L15-L27).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: poly_interp
integer, parameter :: rk=selected_real_kind(12)
real(rk) :: nodes(0:2), values(0:2), offsets(0:2), y(0:1), correction(0:1)
nodes = [0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk]
values = nodes**2
offsets = nodes-0.5_rk
call poly_interp(y,correction,offsets,values,2,1)
```

Uncompiled calling sketch. The analytic value/first derivative at 0.5 are 0.25 and 1, but no comparison was run. Match selected_real_kind(12) consistently with the external routine. A small final correction does not certify interpolation error, and duplicate or nearly coincident input abscissae need independent validation.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The inspected ordered-grid branch of grid_interp selects a local n+1-point stencil for each target, shifts its abscissae to that target and calls poly_interp. Stencil changes produce a piecewise-polynomial interpolation scheme (E1a), without an established spline smoothness condition at transitions. Both values and requested derivatives are copied into the target matrix. The wrapper checks some sizes and rejects extrapolation outside a scale-dependent tolerance. The unordered-grid sorting path is present but outside this source review. Its reported dymax is updated as a maximum of signed dy values starting from zero, rather than absolute corrections, so negative corrections can be hidden; it is not an absolute error estimate. Use distinct strictly ordered samples, in-range ordered targets and 0 <= nd <= n. No grid interpolation or derivative error check was executed.

External ordered-grid interpolation wrapper. n is local polynomial degree, nin >= n+1, nd is derivative limit, nout <= mxdout. xin(nin), fin(nin), xout(mxdout), fout(mxdout,0:nd), dymax(0:nd) use selected_real_kind(12). fout(:,0) stores values and later columns derivatives. Check ifail before using outputs; dymax has the signed-correction limitation. Link poly_interp, and also sort for the compiled unordered branch even when not used.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL grid_interp(n, nd, nin, xin, fin, nout, xout, fout, dymax, ifail, mxdout)
```

Argument declarations: [grid_interp.f90:18–40](https://github.com/jlm785/polynomial_interpolation/blob/5147f4797ce8f7278bcc34e8b1147f45e5283357/grid_interp.f90#L18-L40).

external :: grid_interp

real(rk) :: nodes(4), values(4), queries(2), result(2,0:1), indicator(0:1)
nodes = [0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk,3.0_rk]
values = nodes**2
queries = [0.5_rk,1.5_rk]

```

[README.md](https://github.com/dengwirda/PPR/blob/3c2246463d5de14f492139987bd84978b84e86ea/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `909263da10892118d46a61d1041cc131afe854beb523027749c5fc9a597ef8fa`.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

The reviewed PCM path of ppr_1d reconstructs piecewise-constant cell profiles from cell means and remaps them by integrating profile/target-cell overlaps. rcon1d dispatches to pcm, which copies each cell mean as its constant coefficient; rmap1d/xmap1d selects that one-coefficient representation, and imap1d evaluates integral basis differences and divides the accumulated mass by target-cell width. A subsequent compensated-sum defect correction adjusts an extremal target mean. This establishes a degree-zero piecewise-polynomial reconstruction/remapping path in E1a; it is not point-sample interpolation or a standalone PDE integrator. Restrict this review to ndof=1, PCM, compatible monotone source/target edges over the same domain and positive cell widths. The higher-order PLM/PPM/PQM and limiter implementations were not fully reviewed. Workspaces and all option fields must be initialized; the init methods dereference opts even though declared optional. No conservation, positivity or remapping-accuracy test was run.

Module routine reconstructing cell moments. For the reviewed PCM path, use ndof=1, opts%cell_meth=pcm_method and initialized work/options. fdat and fhat have shape (1,nvar,npos-1); delx is positive spacing, length one for uniform grids or npos-1 otherwise. Supply nvar-element boundary arrays even though PCM does not use their values. No status flag is returned.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL rcon1d(npos, nvar, ndof, delx, fdat, bclo, bchi, fhat, work, opts, tCPU)
```

Module conservative remapper using source/target edge coordinates, not cell centers. With reviewed PCM and ndof=1, fdat is (1,nvar,npos-1) and fnew is (1,nvar,nnew-1). Supply same-domain compatible edge arrays, rmap_work initialized for the source grid, rmap_opts and boundary arrays. Pass opts to work%init despite its optional declaration. Routine assumes valid shapes and geometry and returns no status.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL rmap1d(npos, nnew, nvar, ndof, xpos, xnew, fdat, fnew, bclo, bcup, work, opts, tCPU)
```

Argument declarations: [src/rmap1d.f90:65–76](https://github.com/dengwirda/PPR/blob/3c2246463d5de14f492139987bd84978b84e86ea/src/rmap1d.f90#L65-L76).

Argument declarations: [src/ppr_1d.f90:120–131](https://github.com/dengwirda/PPR/blob/3c2246463d5de14f492139987bd84978b84e86ea/src/ppr_1d.f90#L120-L131).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use ppr_1d
type(rmap_work) :: work
type(rmap_opts) :: opts
type(rcon_ends) :: lower(1), upper(1)
real(dp) :: old_edges(3), new_edges(2), old_mean(1,1,2), new_mean(1,1,1)
opts%edge_meth = p1e_method
opts%cell_meth = pcm_method
opts%cell_lims = null_limit
opts%wall_lims = null_limit
lower = rcon_ends(bcon_loose,0.0_dp,0.0_dp)
upper = lower
old_edges = [0.0_dp,1.0_dp,2.0_dp]
new_edges = [0.0_dp,2.0_dp]
old_mean(1,1,:) = [1.0_dp,3.0_dp]
call work%init(3,1,opts)
call rmap1d(3,2,1,1,old_edges,new_edges,old_mean,new_mean, &
            lower,upper,work,opts)
call work%free()
```

Uncompiled PCM calling sketch; the analytic coarse-cell average is two. The inputs are cell means, and conservation compares width-weighted sums. Compile the module with preprocessing enabled and its included source files available; do not compile the include fragments as unrelated standalone modules. No higher-order limiter, transport example or numerical check is demonstrated.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

LININTERPOL searches for neighboring abscissae and evaluates an affine weighted pair, using a saved interval index for subsequent calls. The implemented interpolation is univariate piecewise linear. Despite header prose promising zero outside the table, those returns/assignments are commented out; search conditions may evaluate negative/out-of-range elements and the final formula extrapolates after clamping. The nold<1 check does not reject a one-point table. Even an in-range query on a two-point table can first read beyond the upper end because the saved-index clamp sets nold-1 then accesses ilastnum+1. Resetting ILASTVAL sets ILASTNUM=-1; a subsequent upward search can begin at -2 and read a negative index even for an in-range query. More table points do not repair this. The sketch records the interface only; the search requires repair and checked testing before use. This review does not establish flux conservation or review the spectral-resampling dispatcher.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `baa2789e0607b063737e4d52759fa21c3e1ef9a7`.

[src/fortran/LINinterpol.f90](https://github.com/neutrinomuon/PyFluxconserving/blob/baa2789e0607b063737e4d52759fa21c3e1ef9a7/src/fortran/LINinterpol.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `56de8c84c07dfdca1b3304b7a08cff33d6a5acdb7990310d3b082b8d69167d13`.

[src/fortran/DataTypes.f90](https://github.com/neutrinomuon/PyFluxconserving/blob/baa2789e0607b063737e4d52759fa21c3e1ef9a7/src/fortran/DataTypes.f90)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `e1b320dd03e169ce8e4fd01e234a1e96685dfc0888f3b2b97cbcaedb80156b48`.

Public entry point `LINinterpol`: [src/fortran/LINinterpol.f90:45–212](https://github.com/neutrinomuon/PyFluxconserving/blob/baa2789e0607b063737e4d52759fa21c3e1ef9a7/src/fortran/LINinterpol.f90#L45-L212).

External subroutine using numeric RP=8 and IB=4 kinds from ModDataType. Table/query/output vectors use dummy lower bound zero; NOLD_VEC/NXYVALUE are explicit lengths. ILASTVAL is input/output (negative resets saved search state), ISKEEPON is output and VERBOSITY optional. An explicit interface is required.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL LINinterpol(XX_VALUE, YY_VALUE, NXYVALUE, XOLD_VEC, YOLD_VEC, &
     NOLD_VEC, ILASTVAL, ISKEEPON, VERBOSITY)
```

Argument declarations: [src/fortran/LINinterpol.f90:45–59](https://github.com/neutrinomuon/PyFluxconserving/blob/baa2789e0607b063737e4d52759fa21c3e1ef9a7/src/fortran/LINinterpol.f90#L45-L59).

Argument declarations: [src/fortran/DataTypes.f90:15–22](https://github.com/neutrinomuon/PyFluxconserving/blob/baa2789e0607b063737e4d52759fa21c3e1ef9a7/src/fortran/DataTypes.f90#L15-L22).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

use ModDataType, only: rp,ib
! Supply the linked explicit interface including OPTIONAL VERBOSITY.
real(rp) :: x(0:2), y(0:2), query(0:0), value(0:0)
integer(ib) :: last,status
x=[0.0_rp,1.0_rp,2.0_rp]; y=2.0_rp*x
query=[0.5_rp]; last=-999_ib
call LINinterpol(query,value,1_ib,x,y,3_ib,last,status,0_ib)
! Inspect STATUS, but it does not certify bounds safety or accuracy.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is an interface sketch, not a recommended safe general interpolator. The source search/bounds findings need repair and checked testing. Saved ILASTNUM makes the core nonreentrant; resetting ILASTVAL is essential after changing tables. Numeric kind constants are compiler-dependent. Direct callers supply lengths hidden by F2PY.

**H2a1b2 — source-reviewed**

The external GAUSSLEGENDREQUADRATURE routine generates successive n-point Gauss-Legendre rules with polynomial recurrence/Newton root refinement, linearly interpolates tabulated X/Y at those nodes and returns the last weighted sum. This is nonautomatic finite-interval quadrature of gridded data, not a callback integrator or accuracy-controlled algorithm. N_INT is the last quadrature order, not a tolerance. Source finding: an optional-argument fallback computes N_INTERATIONS, but the actual loop uses N_INT directly; omitting it references an absent optional argument. Orders below one leave Z undefined. LININTERPOL status is ignored and its indexing is unsafe even for in-range queries: resetting its saved index to -1 can start the upward search at -2. The calling sketch does not repair this. The rule generator caps Newton refinement at ten steps without reporting nonconvergence. This review does not promote the larger INTEGRALALL dispatcher or every branch to source-reviewed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `bab28287f29298c701e4c8bbc7d881f62c97fd4a`.

External subroutine using ModDataType::RP=8 and IB=4 numeric kind values. X/Y are arrays of N_VALUES samples, A/B endpoints and Z a scalar output. Always pass positive N_INT explicitly for this revision and keep all quadrature nodes strictly within a valid sorted input table. There is no returned status/error estimate.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL GaussLegendreQuadrature(X, Y, N_VALUES, Z, A, B, N_INT)
```

Argument declarations: [src/fortran/GaussLegendreQuadrature.f90:41–75](https://github.com/neutrinomuon/PyIntegral/blob/bab28287f29298c701e4c8bbc7d881f62c97fd4a/src/fortran/GaussLegendreQuadrature.f90#L41-L75).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use ModDataType, only: rp, ib
! Provide an explicit interface matching the linked declarations (N_INT is OPTIONAL).
real(rp) :: x(3), y(3), value
x = [-1.0_rp,0.0_rp,2.0_rp]; y = 2.0_rp*x+1.0_rp
call GaussLegendreQuadrature(x,y,3_ib,value,0.0_rp,1.0_rp,10_ib)
! Analytic integral of 2*x+1 over [0,1] is 2.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The fragment requires the explicit interface, ModDataType and linked LINinterpol. Positive N_INT and sorted distinct samples are application requirements, not reliable validation supplied by this code. More quadrature nodes cannot recover information missing from the sampled input. No result, Newton convergence or repeated-call safety was checked.

**G2e1 — source-reviewed**

The standard qp_problem constructor copies and Cholesky-factorizes a positive-definite quadratic matrix, stores its inverse triangular factor, and records linear equality/inequality rows. solve_standard_qp packs constraints and calls the private qpgen2 active-set implementation. The reviewed driver starts at the unconstrained quadratic minimizer, selects violated constraints, computes primal/dual steps, adds constraints with Givens rotations and removes constraints when a dual step requires it. G2e1 records positive-definite-Hessian quadratic programming; no indefinite or merely semidefinite extension is inferred. The objective is 0.5*x-transpose*P*x - x-transpose*q, with A*x=b and C*x>=d; sign and row orientation matter. The constructor checks dimensions but does not propagate TRTRI INFO, and its Cholesky call has no returned err argument. The unconstrained wrapper branch sets X and success but never assigns result%obj; the sketch therefore uses a constrained case. The boolean success loses detailed driver failure information, so validate returned feasibility/stationarity independently. Compact storage, least-squares/LASSO variants and external numerical kernels are not audited. No QP or author tests were executed. The linked inequality test transposes C despite the constructor row-storage interface; that example orientation needs checking and is not copied into the sketch.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `cf3293da6629c6755df77578cca22cc4b33e4ba0`.

Public generic constructor for the dense standard problem. P(n,n) must be symmetric positive definite, q(n) gives the SUBTRACTED linear term. Optional A/b and C/d must occur in pairs, with one constraint per ROW. All arrays use dp=selected_real_kind(15,307). The constructor stores a factorization rather than the original P; reconstruct the object when changing P and preserve originals for residual/KKT checks.

Usage:

```fortran
problem = qp_problem(P, q, A=A, b=b, C=C, d=d)
```

Public generic, scoped to the standard qp_problem overload. Input problem is INTENT(IN); private working copies are modified. Returns OptimizeResult with x, multipliers y (equalities followed by inequalities), obj and success for a constrained solve. Check success before using outputs. The unconstrained return path leaves obj unset.

result = solve(problem)
```

type(qp_problem) :: problem

Use the constructor, not raw component assignment to an unfactorized qp_problem. Build with the pinned project dependencies (stdlib, BLAS and BerkeleyLab/assert); dependency versions are not fully pinned by its manifest. The author test is linked as evidence, not claimed to pass here. The sketch avoids the unconstrained objective-field defect; it does not certify active-set update paths. SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `9729d55f653ded96cb3f3a90f181aa50f04454c0133e4c37afe615dd8b84146f`.

**G1b2 — source-reviewed**

The inspected executable minimizes a finite maximum of component functions, a generally nonsmooth multivariate objective. functmu builds a log-sum-exp smoothing from value-only functs callbacks, and MAINBOX performs derivative-free line searches while adapting the smoothing parameter. This supports the G1b2 leaf. Despite the linearly constrained minimax paper cited in the header, the inspected interface exposes neither bounds nor a general linear-constraint callback or matrix; no G2h2 claim is inferred from the citation. Exponent clipping and a small-sum floor are implementation safeguards, not a checked stable log-sum-exp algorithm for every magnitude. The supplied Hald-Madsen rational-approximation problem can encounter denominator issues; its reported optimum was not reproduced. No convergence, minimax accuracy or example execution was checked.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870`.

[CODE/problem.f](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/problem.f)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `ba3a2f1f553d91b4fc6a8bf18aa1700ad7148d2906f155553767da7f63d43cac`.

Program entry point `minmax`: [CODE/main.f90:1–57](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/main.f90#L1-L57).

Implementation helper `functmu`: [CODE/main.f90:62–96](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/main.f90#L62-L96).

Public entry point `MAINBOX`: [CODE/SDMINMAX.f:22–90](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/SDMINMAX.f#L22-L90).

External finite-minimax search routine. x is the initial REAL*8 point and is overwritten; mu is the smoothing parameter set/adapted by the routine. The caller allocates scratch vectors and matrices, including FSTOP(n+1), XFSTOP(n,n+1) and FINIT(n,2). Linked FUNCTMU/FUNCTS and COMMON blocks provide objective data; no callback argument, bounds or linear-constraint matrix is present despite the MAINBOX name.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL MAINBOX(N, X, D, D1, Z, Z1, XOLD, NUM_ITER, DOLDALFA, &
             IPRINT, DCONV, FSTOP, XFSTOP, FINIT, mu)
```

Argument declarations: [CODE/SDMINMAX.f:22–45](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/SDMINMAX.f#L22-L45).

Author example (not run): [CODE/main.f90:1–46](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/main.f90#L1-L46).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
! Follow program minmax for problem/COMMON initialization and allocation.
! Initialize X through your problem STARTP before entering MAINBOX.
call MAINBOX(N, X, D, D1, Z, Z1, XOLD, NUM_ITER, DOLDALFA, &
             IPRINT, DCONV, FSTOP, XFSTOP, FINIT, mu)
```

Calling sketch only. Supply the separately linked set_dimension, STARTP and FUNCTS problem routines and retain the FUNCTMU smoothing adapter from CODE/main.f90 (or extract it when writing a new main program). Preserve COMMON-block types and layout; allocate workspace exactly as in the driver. The name MAINBOX does not establish a bound-constrained API. The supplied rational-approximation example and smoothing accuracy remain untested.

Implementation evidence `MAINBOX`: [CODE/SDMINMAX.f:112–156](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/SDMINMAX.f#L112-L156).

Implementation evidence `MAINBOX`: [CODE/SDMINMAX.f:298–325](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/SDMINMAX.f#L298-L325).

Callback `functs`: [CODE/problem.f:35–52](https://github.com/DerivativeFreeLibrary/SDMINMAX/blob/27a938c530b5a8b4bddc3f6c3dc56ab655e90870/CODE/problem.f#L35-L52).

**G — documentation-reviewed**

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `7d3f57d39de38bfb687a551fef26a86700a8ab7f`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `4bad2896767a478fb2ecffd7451e8f790689be84fe98cbc9abb0ba0105ca1172`.

**G2h3b — source-reviewed**

sksolve relaxes nonlinear inequalities g(x)<=gamma, restores feasibility and reduces gamma while searching within variable bounds. Equalities require an appropriate inequality encoding; the inspected public interface has no separate equality count or equality flag. The pinned source selects SK_RESTTYPE=2, a function-value compass restoration; the ALGENCAN branch returns with instructions to uncomment code, so it is not active merely by changing that selector. Compass and SDS improvement paths are active; Nelder-Mead, BOBYQA and DFO branches return before commented implementations. G2h3b is the supported nonlinear-constraint scope. A smooth or fully general nonsmooth leaf is withheld because the reviewed material does not establish a matching regularity contract for all active paths; derivative-free alone does not imply nonsmooth convergence. The toy file describes HS6 as an equality but exposes one signed constraint value, so its encoding must be checked before reuse as an equality driver. No program was run.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `7d3f57d39de38bfb687a551fef26a86700a8ab7f`.

Module interface `skinny::SK_RESTTYPE / sksolve`: [skinny.f90:22–25](https://github.com/fsobral/skinny/blob/7d3f57d39de38bfb687a551fef26a86700a8ab7f/skinny.f90#L22-L25).

Public entry point `skinny::sksolve`: [skinny.f90:94–181](https://github.com/fsobral/skinny/blob/7d3f57d39de38bfb687a551fef26a86700a8ab7f/skinny.f90#L94-L181).

Public module subroutine for constrained minimization with relaxed constraints. x is an in-place REAL(8) point, l/u are bounds and m is the constraint count. The interface returns f, maxinfeas, evaluation counts and a flag. Problem evaluators are separately linked routines, not callback arguments in this call.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL sksolve(n, x, l, u, m, feas, opti, gammadec, reffort, delta, &
             sfactor, verbose, uoptmtype, f, maxinfeas, fcnt, gcnt, flag)
```

Argument declarations: [skinny.f90:181–200](https://github.com/fsobral/skinny/blob/7d3f57d39de38bfb687a551fef26a86700a8ab7f/skinny.f90#L181-L200).

Author example (not run): [runeng.f90:105–131](https://github.com/fsobral/skinny/blob/7d3f57d39de38bfb687a551fef26a86700a8ab7f/runeng.f90#L105-L131).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use skinny, only: sksolve
! Link your evalobjfun/evalconstr and initialization routines.
! Initialize x, bounds, relaxation controls and method selection.
call sksolve(n, x, l, u, m, feas, opti, gammadec, reffort, delta, &
             sfactor, verbose, uoptmtype, f, maxinfeas, fcnt, gcnt, flag)
```

Calling sketch only. Follow runeng.f90 and the problem interfaces in toyprob.f90, but do not treat the toy signed-constraint example as a verified equality-constraint driver. The pinned SK_RESTTYPE default selects compass restoration. Several advertised solver branches contain stubs/commented implementations, so changing a selector does not establish that the requested optimizer works. Check flag and maxinfeas. Not built or run for this catalog.

**C10a3 — source-reviewed**

The inspected real SBESSJ evaluates spherical j_n(x), choosing a power series for |x|<=0.78*n and upward recurrence from sin(x)/x and (sin(x)/x-cos(x))/x otherwise. At x=0 the series returns j_0=1 and j_n=0 for n>0. C10a3 (real argument, real order) is used for the half-integer cylindrical-Bessel subset: j_n(x)=sqrt(pi/(2*x))*J_(n+1/2)(x) for positive x (NIST DLMF 10.47.3, https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.47.E3). The procedure exposes only nonnegative integer spherical n, not arbitrary real cylindrical orders, Y/Hankel or modified I/K functions. Negative order, a flagged low-accuracy positive-x region for n>50, and series nonconvergence print diagnostics and STOP. The low-accuracy guard uses x rather than abs(x), so negative-x reliability is not established by that guard. Series stopping uses an absolute term threshold and a finite 20+2*n budget; it supplies neither a returned error estimate nor a status code. Precision/accuracy claims in comments/README were not reproduced. Complex and quad variants and the comparison implementation remain outside this source review. No Bessel value or recurrence residual was executed.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `90759662246614ffb3bbcfaa770b0bc98b9fb4a2`.

Public entry point `sbessj`: [sbessj.f90:19–155](https://github.com/jlm785/spherical_bessel_fortran/blob/90759662246614ffb3bbcfaa770b0bc98b9fb4a2/sbessj.f90#L19-L155).

External real spherical-Bessel function. n is default INTEGER and must be nonnegative; x and function result use selected_real_kind(12), called REAL64 locally (not an ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constant). Declare that exact return kind in an explicit interface or typed EXTERNAL declaration. Returns one j_n(x) value, with no derivative/status. Some invalid or low-accuracy cases STOP.

Usage:

```fortran
value = sbessj(n, x)
```

Argument declarations: [sbessj.f90:31–42](https://github.com/jlm785/spherical_bessel_fortran/blob/90759662246614ffb3bbcfaa770b0bc98b9fb4a2/sbessj.f90#L31-L42).

Author example (not run): [test_bessel.f90:5–31](https://github.com/jlm785/spherical_bessel_fortran/blob/90759662246614ffb3bbcfaa770b0bc98b9fb4a2/test_bessel.f90#L5-L31).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
integer, parameter :: rk=selected_real_kind(12)
real(rk), external :: sbessj
real(rk) :: at_origin, value
at_origin=sbessj(0,0.0_rk)
value=sbessj(2,1.0_rk)
```

Uncompiled fragment; at_origin should be one, but no result was checked. Build/link sbessj.f90 with compatible default INTEGER and selected_real_kind(12). This is the spherical j_n function: an integer argument n corresponds to cylindrical order n+1/2, not J_n. A matching kind alone does not certify the author accuracy claim. The supplied interactive comparison program embeds a separately licensed reference routine and was not run.

Not built or run for this catalog. Source-reviewed mappings identify inspected driver/implementation paths and calling interfaces, not complete dependency audits or numerical verification. The earlier documentation review remains available.

**E1a — source-reviewed**

SPLIFT assembles/factors a tridiagonal system for nodal second derivatives with user endpoint relations, solves it and recovers first derivatives; SPLINT locates intervals by hunt/bisection and evaluates cubic values/first/second derivatives. E1a records interpolating piecewise cubics, not smoothing. Use at least four strictly increasing nodes for the reviewed fit path. ISX=1 reuses the factorization only when nodes, workspace and endpoint coefficients are unchanged; validation is skipped on that reuse path. Success is IERR/KERR=1, not zero. SPLINT extrapolates the end cubic and returns KERR=2; equal adjacent nodes can STOP. N<4 fitting returns zero derivatives and IERR=2 rather than the normal cubic result. No interpolation, derivative or extrapolation accuracy was run; integration through SPLIQ is outside this mapping.

External spline constructor. REAL(selected_real_kind(12)) arrays X/Y/YP/YPP length N, W(N,3), default-INTEGER N/IERR/ISX. ISX=0 first call. Endpoint relations are YPP(1)=A1*YPP(2)+B1 and YPP(N)=AN*YPP(N-1)+BN; all zeros give natural endpoints. Check IERR=1.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL splift(x,y,yp,ypp,n,w,ierr,isx,a1,b1,an,bn)
```

Argument declarations: [splift.f90:29–52](https://github.com/jlm785/spline_interpolation_fortran/blob/f6068b941876e9df2930eeae60017a5e9491780b/splift.f90#L29-L52).

Public entry point `splint`: [splint.f90:16–168](https://github.com/jlm785/spline_interpolation_fortran/blob/f6068b941876e9df2930eeae60017a5e9491780b/splint.f90#L16-L168).

External evaluation of spline defined by X/Y/YPP. XI/YI/YPI/YPPI length NI; returns values and two derivatives. Queries may be unordered. KERR=1 normal, 2 extrapolation, 3 invalid NI. Preserve matching X/Y/YPP and check statuses before use.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL splint(x,y,ypp,n,xi,yi,ypi,yppi,ni,kerr)
```

Argument declarations: [splint.f90:29–43](https://github.com/jlm785/spline_interpolation_fortran/blob/f6068b941876e9df2930eeae60017a5e9491780b/splint.f90#L29-L43).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
integer, parameter :: rk=selected_real_kind(12), n=4
external :: splift, splint
integer :: ierr, kerr
real(rk) :: x(n), y(n), yp(n), ypp(n), w(n,3)
real(rk) :: xi(1), yi(1), d1(1), d2(1)
x=[0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk,3.0_rk]
y=x
call splift(x,y,yp,ypp,n,w,ierr,0,0.0_rk,0.0_rk,0.0_rk,0.0_rk)
if (ierr /= 1) error stop "spline fit failed"
xi=1.5_rk
call splint(x,y,ypp,n,xi,yi,d1,d2,1,kerr)
if (kerr /= 1) error stop "spline evaluation not in range"
```

Uncompiled in-range linear-data fragment. Expected value 1.5, first derivative one and second derivative zero were not checked. Link both external routines with matching kinds; SPLIQ is not needed for this sketch. Only reuse W with ISX=1 when the documented node/boundary conditions are unchanged. No Numerical Recipes-derived search licensing/accuracy audit was performed.

**E2a — source-reviewed**

The inspected structured-grid path prepares four tensor-product bilinear weights from normalized x/y coordinates, caches them by a formatted coordinate key, and applies them to four supplied values. E2a records gridded bivariate interpolation; the type does not fetch a full field or perform three-/four-coordinate interpolation (higher-rank values carry extra fields). Important source defects prevent a general-use recommendation: REAL(8) regular-grid preparation uses FLOOR without the required one-based offset and leaves the fourth corner second index zero by writing corner 3 twice; REAL(4) uses CEILING but excludes the lower endpoint and accepts some cells past the final valid interval. apply calls prepare on a cache miss but computes its result only in the ELSE branch, leaving the first return undefined unless prepare is called explicitly. apply neither guards outside points nor checks value-array extents. Its corner order is (lower-left, lower-right, upper-right, upper-left) mapped to input positions (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2), not the usual rectangular-field order. The sketch is a restricted REAL(4), strictly interior, explicitly prepared interface illustration. Curvilinear location/inversion and dependencies are not audited. No interpolation or defect was reproduced by execution.

Public generic type-bound initializer. Scope here is private REAL(4) one-dimensional-axis binding: x(nx), y(ny), optional default-INTEGER cache_size. It copies axes into REAL(8) storage and creates the cache. Regular axes must be increasing and equidistant, each with at least two points; no validation enforces this. Curvilinear overloads exist but are not the illustrated path.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL interp%init(x, y, cache_size)
```

Public generic for caching a point. The illustrated REAL(4) binding accepts scalar x/y and mutates the cache. Call explicitly before apply to avoid its unassigned first-return path. Boundary handling has documented defects, so the sketch uses a strictly interior point of a two-by-two grid.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL interp%prepare(x, y)
```

Public generic, scoped to the REAL(4) scalar-field binding. Supply a two-by-two array in the source corner order: (1,1)=LL, (2,1)=LR, (1,2)=UR, (2,2)=UL, plus REAL(4) query coordinates. It mutates the cache; a prior prepare call is required for a defined return. Do not pass a conventional field slice without checking the swapped upper-corner ordering.

Usage:

```fortran
value = interp%apply(enclose_values, x, y)
```

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use bilinear_interpolator_mod, only: bilinear_interpolator_type
type(bilinear_interpolator_type) :: interp
real(4) :: x(2), y(2), corners(2,2), value
x=[0.0,1.0]
y=[0.0,1.0]
call interp%init(x,y)
call interp%prepare(0.25,0.5)
if (interp%is_outside(0.25,0.5)) error stop "point classified outside"

corners(1,1)=0.0
corners(2,1)=1.0
corners(1,2)=3.0

Uncompiled restricted fragment, not a checked or recommended general driver until the source defects are fixed. It assumes default REAL is kind 4, matches the REAL(4) overload explicitly and precomputes the cache. Expected value is 1.25; no comparison was performed. The author example instead needs external WRF data/projection dependencies and passes an ordinary rectangular slice, whose upper-corner order differs from apply. REAL(8) regular grids have separate indexing defects. Formatted coordinate keys use to_string(...,4) in a 30-character buffer; collision/rounding behavior and dependency implementation were not audited.

**H2a — documentation-reviewed**

The README documents Jacobi, generalized Laguerre and Hermite rules using iterative polynomial-root methods. The author notes that newer rule-generation packages may offer advantages; no comparative accuracy or speed is asserted here.

Reviewed 2026-11-03 at `b36291d94ffa8a81e5e8aed6d7afb37bc4c0b0e7`.

[README.md](https://github.com/ivan-pi/stroud_quad/blob/b36291d94ffa8a81e5e8aed6d7afb37bc4c0b0e7/README.md)
SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `ccded9963dcec14e1edc54b1f594936ab3dbf479186e99e3f120edd443fed06a`.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

The reviewed HERMIT generator constructs Gauss-Hermite nodes and weights for the exp(-x*x) weight: initial root estimates, Newton corrections via HROOT/HRECUR, mirrored nodes/weights, and Gamma-based normalization. H2c records quadrature rule construction, not an adaptive integral evaluator. HROOT uses at most ten Newton iterations with no returned convergence flag; derivative/polynomial values used in weights are from the last pre-update evaluation. The initial-root expression differs from the formula in its comment, and 2**(N-1) uses default INTEGER arithmetic, which can overflow for higher orders. It prints node diagnostics and performs no order/overflow validation. Only modest positive orders are illustrated. Jacobi/Laguerre generators and numerical moment checks are outside this review.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `b36291d94ffa8a81e5e8aed6d7afb37bc4c0b0e7`.

Public quad_mod rule generator. NN default INTEGER, X(NN)/A(NN) REAL64, optional REAL64 EPS (default machine epsilon). Produces descending/mirrored Hermite roots and weights; for integrating a weighted function compute sum(A*f(X)). There is no convergence/status output.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL hermit(nn, x, a, eps)
```

Argument declarations: [quad_mod.f90:326–334](https://github.com/ivan-pi/stroud_quad/blob/b36291d94ffa8a81e5e8aed6d7afb37bc4c0b0e7/quad_mod.f90#L326-L334).

Author example (not run): [quad_driver.f90:25–27](https://github.com/ivan-pi/stroud_quad/blob/b36291d94ffa8a81e5e8aed6d7afb37bc4c0b0e7/quad_driver.f90#L25-L27).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
use quad_mod, only: wp, hermit
real(wp) :: nodes(4), weights(4), moment
call hermit(4,nodes,weights)
moment=sum(weights*nodes**2)
```

Uncompiled modest-order fragment for the exp(-x*x)-weighted second moment; expected sqrt(pi)/2 was not checked. The routine generates a fixed rule, not error-controlled integration. Check node/weight moments and convergence before relying on results; higher orders risk integer/exponential overflow and the ten-iteration budget has no status.

Implementation helper `quad_mod::hroot`: [quad_mod.f90:375–392](https://github.com/ivan-pi/stroud_quad/blob/b36291d94ffa8a81e5e8aed6d7afb37bc4c0b0e7/quad_mod.f90#L375-L392).

**G1b2 — source-reviewed**

SUBPLX sorts step scales, partitions coordinates into subspaces and calls SIMPLX for derivative-free simplex minimization, repeating until its relative coordinate/step test is satisfied or a limit is returned. The nonsmooth unconstrained class records this local search, not global optimization. Unlike older comments, this fork has no MODE argument and always initializes default options through SUBOPT. COMMON and SAVE state make nested/concurrent use unsafe without isolation. This review does not establish noisy-objective performance or inspect the entire R bridge.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `4808b7103490cf6533d9240301633f38cb4246b6`.

Public entry point `SUBPLX`: [src/subplx.f:1–216](https://github.com/kingaa/subplex/blob/4808b7103490cf6533d9240301633f38cb4246b6/src/subplx.f#L1-L216).

External objective-only minimizer with DOUBLE PRECISION F(N,X). X is overwritten, FX is the resulting cost, NFE the evaluation count. Allocate WORK >= 2*N+NSMAX*(NSMAX+4)+1 and IWORK >= N+INT(N/NSMIN), with default NSMAX=MIN(5,N), NSMIN=MIN(2,N).

Usage:

```fortran
CALL SUBPLX(F, N, TOL, MAXNFE, SCALE, X, FX, NFE, WORK, IWORK, IFLAG)
```

Argument declarations: [src/subplx.f:1–7](https://github.com/kingaa/subplex/blob/4808b7103490cf6533d9240301633f38cb4246b6/src/subplx.f#L1-L7).

Argument declarations: [src/subplx.f:29–80](https://github.com/kingaa/subplex/blob/4808b7103490cf6533d9240301633f38cb4246b6/src/subplx.f#L29-L80).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
! N > 0; declare F DOUBLE PRECISION EXTERNAL and allocate documented work arrays.
scale(1) = -1.0d0  ! common initial step magnitude for every coordinate
iflag = 0
call subplx(f,n,1.0d-6,10000,scale,x,fx,nfe,work,iwork,iflag)
! IFLAG=0 tolerance; 1 machine limit; -1 evaluation budget; -2 invalid input.
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use positive dimensions, a nonnegative tolerance, positive evaluation budget and nonzero representable initial steps. This fork does not expose the old MODE restart/custom-option API. Compile the supporting routines/BLAS; this is the Fortran core of an R package.

## triasymq

**License: BSD-3-Clause core; modified BSD notice for some helpers**

COPYING gives the standard three-clause BSD notice for the Gimbutas/Xiao core. Its separate notice for legeexps.f and prini.f adds a requirement to mark and date modifications. A single BSD-3-Clause expression would omit that extra helper condition; no uniform SPDX expression is asserted for the repository. The inspected triasymq source refers to this COPYING file.

**H2b — documentation-reviewed**

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `f3c46d813307b8dd7feebb6bf34023af1bd5fee19bb8543d1104abd5321516db`.

**H2c — source-reviewed**

The inspected triasymq entry retrieves tabulated reference-triangle nodes and weights, expands the D3 symmetry and maps them affinely to caller-supplied vertices. trianmap rescales weights to the absolute triangle area. This is a fixed-rule service returning nodes/weights, not an adaptive integrand-callback interface. The supported requested polynomial degree is 1..50, distinct from the returned node count (up to 453 according to the table). The wrapper ignores its internal ier, so validate degree before calling and supply a nondegenerate triangle and adequately sized arrays. The internal explicit-shape quaequad dummy uses the incoming nptsout value before overwriting it: initialize numnodes to the supplied capacity rather than relying on the author driver uninitialized variable. Tables and expansion/mapping paths were inspected, but all rule moments, degrees and claimed extended-precision construction accuracy were not independently verified. Other domains in the repository are outside this source review.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 at `332f5f4b2846bd7345400f5d25ad0650b884fa6f`.

SHA-256 (normalized UTF-8/LF): `0fac0a080e3e9f17b6801d54bf439e9087bb60ca71ea87cf68b95f96a8807a49`.

Public entry point `triasymq`: [triasymq.f:17–83](https://github.com/zgimbutas/triasymq/blob/332f5f4b2846bd7345400f5d25ad0650b884fa6f/triasymq.f#L17-L83).

External REAL*8 triangle quadrature-rule retrieval. vert1,vert2,vert3 each have length two, rnodes has two rows and weights is a vector. Prevalidate degree n in 1..50 and nonzero area, allocate capacity at least 453 for the full range, and initialize numnodes to that capacity. On return use only entries 1:numnodes. No public error flag is returned.

Usage:

```fortran
CALL triasymq(n, vert1, vert2, vert3, rnodes, weights, numnodes)
```

Argument declarations: [triasymq.f:17–22](https://github.com/zgimbutas/triasymq/blob/332f5f4b2846bd7345400f5d25ad0650b884fa6f/triasymq.f#L17-L22).

Author example (not run): [triasymq_dr.f:76–90](https://github.com/zgimbutas/triasymq/blob/332f5f4b2846bd7345400f5d25ad0650b884fa6f/triasymq_dr.f#L76-L90).

Calling sketch (not a checked driver):

```fortran
external :: triasymq
integer :: numnodes
double precision :: v1(2), v2(2), v3(2), nodes(2,453), weights(453), q
v1 = [0.0d0,0.0d0]
v2 = [1.0d0,0.0d0]
v3 = [0.0d0,1.0d0]
numnodes = 453
call triasymq(2,v1,v2,v3,nodes,weights,numnodes)
q = sum(weights(1:numnodes)*nodes(1,1:numnodes)**2)
```

Uncompiled calling sketch for the unit right triangle. The analytic integral of x**2 is 1/12, but no numerical moment was checked. The weights already include triangle-area scaling. Degree two is the requested polynomial degree, not an allocation size. Prevalidate input because the public wrapper does not expose internal errors; this is not adaptive error-controlled integration.

Implementation helper `trianmap`: [triasymq.f:89–126](https://github.com/zgimbutas/triasymq/blob/332f5f4b2846bd7345400f5d25ad0650b884fa6f/triasymq.f#L89-L126).

Implementation helper `quaequad`: [triasymq.f:158–256](https://github.com/zgimbutas/triasymq/blob/332f5f4b2846bd7345400f5d25ad0650b884fa6f/triasymq.f#L158-L256).

**G1b1b — source-reviewed**

The UCMINF core forms an inverse-Hessian search direction, limits its length, performs a soft line search and updates a packed inverse Hessian by BFGS when a curvature test permits it. This mapping is scoped to supplied first derivatives: the R frontend sets GRAD=0 when GR is provided; FDF dispatches objective/gradient through linked C routines evaluating an R environment. The fork removed the FDF callback argument from the Fortran entry. RHO is an opaque runtime handle, not an ordinary user integer work array. This is local smooth unconstrained optimization, not a standalone Fortran callback solver or a certified trust-region method.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 at `3c7b956c057acecddd34ab66d6830ec04ddc1966`.

call ucminf(n,x,dx,eps,maxfun,w,iw,icontr,grad,grstep,rho)
```

Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use the supported R frontend ucminf::ucminf(par, fn, gr=gradient) to construct the runtime state; FN returns a scalar and GR a numeric vector of length N. The R formal arguments and bridge declarations are linked separately. Positive termination codes distinguish small gradient, small step, evaluation budget and stalled line search; inspect the returned message.
